IITM-CR-6C5DBB52.synthesis_remarks:
1. GEOTECHNICAL & USGS CLASSIFICATION (USGS Circular 1325 / Cruden & Varnes 1996):
Forensic field reconnaissance of the Mandi sector confirms an active mass wasting event conforming strictly to the USGS standard definition of a landslide: "A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement."
Under the Cruden & Varnes (1996) two-term taxonomy, the failure is formally designated as: Translational Rock Slide (Rock Block Slide) (Kinematic Movement: Translational Slide, Substrate: Rock, Velocity Rating: Rapid [Class 5, 1.8 m/h to 3 m/min]).

2. CONSEQUENCE RATING & TARGET FACTOR OF SAFETY (CEDD Geoguide 1):
Directly impacting mandi sub-divisional hill road corridor. Under Hong Kong CEDD Geoguide 1 criteria, the slope is classified as Category 2 (Moderate Consequence), requiring a statutory minimum target Factor of Safety FOS >= 1.25 under 10-year return period rainfall (FOS >= 1.15 under extreme storm conditions).

3. KINEMATIC FAILURE MECHANICS, ANATOMY & HYDROGEOLOGY:
Instability is characterized by A landslide mass that moves out, or down and outward, along a relatively planar surface with little rotational movement or backward tilting; frequently controlled by structural discontinuities (bedding, joints, faults). within Phyllite strata under steep cut geometry (55° to 59° (Moderately Stable Cut)). Diagnostic landslide anatomical features (USGS Circular 1325) include an exposed detachment main scarp and depletion mass, open tension crown fissures, and an accumulation toe encroaching upon the corridor. Failure was triggered by antecedent rainfall infiltration inducing transient perched groundwater tables, loss of matric suction in the upper colluvium, and hydrostatic cleft-water pressure along daylighting relict joints (dipping 53° into the cut face).

4. MULTI-BARRIER MITIGATION STRATEGY (LaRiMiT / CEDD GEO Standards):
- Primary Toe Retention (LaRiMiT Cluster 4): Construction of a 13m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H=2.0m, Base B=1.00m) founded on competent bedrock with 100mm PVC weep holes @ 1.2m c/c.
- Internal Ground Reinforcement (LaRiMiT Cluster 5 / CEDD Geoguide 7): Prescribed Soil Nailing Array (Dia. 25 mm (Fe500 High-Yield Deformed Steel), 2.25 m (H) x 2.25 m (V) Square Pattern, length 6.0 m to 9.0 m) with sacrificial pullout verification testing.
- Pore Pressure Relief (LaRiMiT Cluster 3 / CEDD TGN 24): Installation of 15.0 m per borehole (Total 4 Nos. array) sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains inclined at 5° to 10° upward rake for gravity self-cleansing flow to intercept perched seepage, paired with lined crest interceptor drains (0.84 m x 0.61 m).
- Dynamic Impact & NBS Protection: 500 kJ Rating flexible ring net barrier (CEDD GEO Report No. 138 / EOTA EAD 340059-00-0106) in fall zones, combined with Live Vegetated Crib Wall / Timber Cribbing.

5. STATUTORY MAINTENANCE REGIME:
Mandatory Engineer Inspection for Maintenance (EIM) at Every 2 years for Category 1 slopes; every 5 years for Category 2/3 slopes by a Qualified Geotechnical Engineer (Executive / Assistant Engineer) in strict accordance with CEDD Geoguide 5.

plain_language_explanation.summary_title: Active Slope Failure and Roadway Undermining
plain_language_explanation.what_happened: A significant portion of the hillside has detached, causing a landslide that has undermined the road structure.
plain_language_explanation.why_it_happened: The failure is driven by the weak, foliated nature of the local phyllite rock, exacerbated by water infiltration and poor drainage.
plain_language_explanation.property_and_access_impact: The road is partially blocked and structurally compromised, posing a risk of further collapse.
plain_language_explanation.road_and_travel_impact: Passage is obstructed (3.80 m (Single-Lane Traffic Operable)). Vehicles and pedestrians cannot safely transit this point.
plain_language_explanation.ongoing_hazards: Risk of secondary rockfalls and further subsidence of the road pavement.
plain_language_explanation.what_needs_to_be_done: Immediate debris removal, installation of temporary shoring, and long-term slope stabilization using soil nails and drainage.
plain_language_explanation.citizen_safety_advice: Avoid the area, do not park vehicles near the scarp, and follow all traffic diversions.

tier_1_factual_evidence.title: Tier 1: Factual Ground Truth & Telemetry (Objective Past Passive)
tier_1_factual_evidence.description: At Mandi Sector — Hill Road Corridor (Mandi Sector), a detachment scarp of vertical height 7.60 m (upper face 4.90 m inclined at 66°) was surveyed. Saturated shali dolomite & sundernagar quartzite with interbedded phyllitic slate / dharamsala sandstone debris (145.0 m³ in-situ / 181.25 m³ bulked calculated via Simpson's prismoidal rule at 1.25 bulking factor) encroached 2.95 m across the 5.25 m carriageway formation. Roadside drainage was 100% obstructed under active hydrostatic surcharge. Prior to failure, the cut slope was an unprotected excavation. Discontinuities dipping 57° adversely into the slope face were measured with aperture 15–40 mm.

tier_2_analytical_mechanics.title: Tier 2: Analytical Geotechnical Mechanics & FoS (Calibrated Engineering Inferences)
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.description: Under the Cruden & Varnes (1996) and USGS Circular 1325 classification, the failure is designated as a Translational slide transitioning into debris flow Mass Movement (Cruden & Varnes, 1996) within Shali Dolomite & Sundernagar Quartzite with interbedded phyllitic slate / Dharamsala Sandstone strata. Under dry baseline conditions, limit equilibrium stability analysis (Hoek & Bray planar cleft-water mechanics) yields FoS = 1.01 (marginal). During monsoon steady-seepage saturation with active joint cleft-water hydrostatic pressure (zw = 1.2m), calculated FoS drops to 0.60, confirming active shear mobilization along daylighting joint set J1 (slip plane inclined length L_slip = 6.856 m). Following multi-barrier stabilization, post-remediation FoS is verified at 1.54. The site lies in Seismic Zone V (Z = 0.36, ah = 0.09g).
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.disclaimer: Subsurface geotechnical parameters (effective cohesion c' = 14.0 kPa, effective internal friction angle φ' = 28.0°, intact rock UCS = 35.0 MPa, and structural joint dip = 57.0°) are preliminary model estimates and assumptions based on empirical rock mass classifications and regional lithological analogs. These values are strictly subject to confirmatory site investigation, trial-pit logging, and rotary borehole core extraction with laboratory testing prior to detailed engineering design, statutory tendering, or construction authorization.

tier_3_statutory_directives.title: Tier 3: Statutory Remediation Directives & Civil Schedule (Imperative Standards)
tier_3_statutory_directives.description:
1. Construct a 17m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H_stem=2.70m, D_f=1.00m, Base B=1.35m, Top b=0.60m, volume = 67.70 m³ M15 with 40% plums per IS:14458 Part 2), backed by 16.07 m³ filter pack and 26 Nos. weep holes.
2. Install 20 Nos. Ø25mm High-Yield Fe500D soil nails (18 working in 1.8m H × 2.0m V grid + 2 sacrificial pullout verification test nails) drilled to 9.0m depth (180m drill, 190m bar, 18 pads, 91.12 m² wire mesh) per MoRTH Section 3100.
3. Install 5 Nos. × 15m (75.0m total) sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains (Ø75mm, Schedule 80) at 5°–10° upward rake, paired with 25.0m crest saucer catch drain (0.60m × 0.60m), 17.0m roadside drain (0.60m × 0.60m), and 22.0m stepped cascade chute per MoRTH Section 300.
4. Lay 700 GSM coir geotextile netting (100.23 m² with 10% overlap), hydroseeding, and Vetiver grass contour hedges per MoRTH Section 1802.

inspection_regime.frequency: Every 2 years for Category 1 slopes; every 5 years for Category 2/3 slopes
inspection_regime.key_checks: Structural integrity of retaining walls, soil nail head pad displacement, crack gauge monitoring, drainage gradient verification

primary_structural.name: Flexible Debris-Flow Ring Barrier (GEO Report 138 VX/UX Class)
primary_structural.description: Multi-level ring nets anchored across mountain torrents with bottom clearance to retain boulder fronts while passing slurry.

hydrogeological_drainage.name: Stepped Concrete Cascade / Chute Drain
hydrogeological_drainage.description: Energy-dissipating stepped RC flume conveying concentrated water down steep slope faces into valley culverts.

nature_based_solution.name: Deep-Rooting Vetiver Grass Contour Hedges (Chrysopogon zizanioides)
nature_based_solution.description: Dense linear vegetative hedges with 2-3m deep massive fibrous root systems (tensile strength ~75 MPa) providing mechanical soil binding and hydraulic shear enhancement.

usgs_classification.usgs_general_definition: A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement.
usgs_classification.usgs_kinematic_definition: A downslope movement of rock or soil, or both, occurring on the surface of rupture—either curved (rotational slide) or planar (translational slide) rupture—in which much of the material often moves as a coherent or semicoherent mass with little internal deformation.
usgs_classification.material_definition: Soil containing a significant proportion of coarse fragments; 20% to 80% of the particles are greater than 2 mm in size (gravel, cobbles, and boulders).
usgs_classification.movement_definition: Spatially continuous movement in which shear surfaces are short-lived, closely spaced, and usually not preserved; component velocities resemble those in a viscous fluid.

velocity_class.consequences: Loss of life expected; some temporary evacuation possible; structures destroyed.

landslide_anatomy.crown_and_scarp: Undisplaced crown with open extensional crown cracks; distinct steep main scarp exposing rupture surface.
landslide_anatomy.displaced_mass: Depleted mass above planar/rotational surface of rupture, extending downslope into zone of accumulation.
landslide_anatomy.toe_and_foot: Displaced foot advancing beyond toe of rupture surface across roadway/property margin.

geological: Weak, weathered, or fractured rock and soil materials
Adversely oriented structural discontinuities (faults, joints, bedding planes daylighting into cut face)
morphological: Fluvial or wave erosion undermining the slope toe
Tectonic or steep gravitational escarpment oversteepening
physical_trigger: Prolonged antecedent precipitation and high-intensity storm rainfall
Transient perched groundwater table development and loss of matric suction
human_causes: Anthropogenic excavation / toe undercutting for roadway benching or foundation cuts
Surcharge loading at the slope crest (unengineered spoil disposal or building construction)

usgs_classification.standard_reference: USGS Circular 1325 (Highland & Bobrowsky, 2008) & Cruden & Varnes (1996) TRB Special Report 247

bhukosh_geology.citation: Rahul V. et al., 2016. Macro-scale (1:50,000) landslide susceptibility Mapping in parts of toposheets no. 53A/13, 14, Kullu and Mandi districts, Himachal Pradesh. Unpub. GSI report of FS 2015-2016

schedule_metadata.title: Himachal Pradesh Public Works Department (HPSOR 2024-25) & MoRTH Hill Roads Schedule
primary_references: HPPWD Schedule of Rates (HPSOR 2024-25), Government of Himachal Pradesh
MoRTH Specifications for Road and Bridge Works (5th Revision)
IS:14458 Guidelines for Retaining/Breast Walls in Hill Areas
IRC:SP:48:1998 Hill Road Manual (Indian Roads Congress)
CEDD Geoguide 7: Guide to Soil Nail Design and Construction (2023 Edition)
schedule_metadata.applicable_terrain: Himalayan Hill Roads & High Altitude Sectors (Mandi Division)

breast_wall.material: Plum Concrete M15 (40% clean quarry plums 150–300mm)

scenarios.stage_name: Dry Natural Baseline (Zero Cleft-Water Pressure, Peak Shear)
Monsoon Cleft-Water Saturation (Active Joint Pore Pressure, zw=1.2m)
Post-Remediation (Plum Wall M15 + Fe500D Nails + Sub-horizontal Drains)

stability_analysis.seismic_zone_note: Site lies in Seismic Zone V (IS:1893:2016, Zone Factor Z=0.36, ah=0.09g). Permanent stabilization accommodates pseudo-static earthquake coefficient in addition to static surcharge.

items.asset: Highway Carriageway Pavement (WMM + Bituminous Crust)
items.criteria: Full pavement reconstruction over damaged corridor (97.12 m² = 18.5m × 5.25m formation width): Scarification, subgrade re-compaction, 150mm WMM base and 50mm Bituminous Concrete overlay @ ₹1,650/m²

items.asset: Roadside Culvert Headwall & Silt Flushing
items.criteria: High-pressure hydraulic flushing of choked 1.2m dia Hume pipe barrel, masonry headwall reconstruction, and cement pressure grouting of apron cracks

items.asset: Emergency Corridor Traffic Staging & Diversion Safety
items.criteria: Deployment of portable steel crash barriers, solar LED hazard flashers, warning signage, and 24/7 flagger spotters during emergency single-lane transit

items.asset: Regional Corridor Freight Detour & Transit Delay
items.criteria: 1.0 day regional commercial transit disruption: Freight carrier diversion (extra 45 km detour via alternate state highway), commercial idling fuel surcharge, and commuter travel-time delay

indirect_economic_disruption.disclaimer: Macroeconomic user-delay losses are recorded for statistical and disaster impact monitoring; strictly excluded from statutory contractor procurement.

boq_items.description: Hydraulic clearance of fallen colluvium and boulders using excavator, including loading, hauling up to 1000m, and dumping at designated HPPWD spoil site. (In-situ 158.0 m³ × 1.25 bulking = 197.5 m³)
boq_items.short_description: Hydraulic excavation & disposal of debris/boulders (lead 1000m)

boq_items.description: Dressing, trimming, and scarp reprofiling of upper cut slope face above breast wall at 64.0° inclination. (18.5m × 5.89m inclined face = 108.96 m²)
boq_items.short_description: Slope trimming, scarp reprofiling & bench dressing in cut face

boq_items.description: Foundation trench excavation in hard rock for breast wall using pneumatic breaker. (18.5m × 1.41m × 1.08m neat trench)
boq_items.short_description: Foundation trench rock excavation with pneumatic breaker for wall footing

boq_items.description: Construction of Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H=2.91m stem, 1.08m embedment, 1.41m base, 0.6m top) in M15 concrete with 40% clean sound plums (150–300mm). (Footing 28.17 m³ + Stem 54.1 m³)
boq_items.short_description: Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H=2.91m, B=1.41m) in M15 with 40% plums

boq_items.description: Non-woven needle-punched polypropylene geotextile filter fabric (250 GSM) wrapping granular drainage pack behind wall stem, with 300mm overlaps. (77.71 m² wrap)
boq_items.short_description: Non-woven polypropylene geotextile filter fabric (250 GSM) wrapping filter pack

boq_items.description: Free-draining graded granular filter backfill (20–40mm crushed gravel) extending full 2.91m stem height behind breast wall. (18.5m × 2.91m × 0.35m)
boq_items.short_description: Free-draining granular filter backfill (20–40mm crushed gravel) behind wall

boq_items.description: Providing and laying 100mm dia perforated PVC weep hole pipes laid at 1:20 slope in 2 staggered rows, wrapped in geotextile. (28 holes × 1.3m)
boq_items.short_description: 100mm dia PVC weep hole pipes @ 1.2m c/c in 2 staggered rows

boq_items.description: Rotary percussion drilling of 100–110mm dia boreholes for soil nails at 15°–20° rake in weathered rock/colluvium. (20 working nails + 2 sacrificial = 22 holes × 9.0m)
boq_items.short_description: Drilling 100–110mm boreholes for soil nails at 15°–20° rake (22 Nos. × 9.0m)

boq_items.description: Supplying and installing Ø25mm High-Yield Fe500D TMT rebar with centralizers @ 1.8m c/c, with 0.5m threaded head projection. (22 bars × 9.5m)
boq_items.short_description: Ø25mm High-Yield Fe500D steel soil nail bars with centralizers (22 Nos. × 9.5m)

boq_items.description: Pressure grouting of boreholes with neat cement grout (fcu ≥ 30 MPa, W/C = 0.42) including expanding admixture. (22 holes × 9.0m)
boq_items.short_description: Pressure grouting of boreholes with non-shrink cementitious grout (≥30 MPa)

boq_items.description: Cast-in-situ reinforced concrete bearing pads (400×400×200mm M30) and 200×200×16mm galvanized steel bearing plates with lock nuts. (20 permanent working pads)
boq_items.short_description: Cast-in-situ RC bearing pads (400×400×200mm M30) & galvanized plates (20 sets)

boq_items.description: Sacrificial pullout verification proof testing up to 1.5× design pullout load with calibrated hollow-core jack on 2 sacrificial nails.
boq_items.short_description: Sacrificial pullout verification proof testing up to 1.5× design load (2 tests)

boq_items.description: Supplying and installing high-tensile flexible diamond steel wire mesh (3.0mm wire, 65×65mm mesh, 50 kN/m) bolted across nail heads to prevent colluvial ravelling.
boq_items.short_description: High-tensile diamond steel wire mesh (3mm wire, 65×65mm, 50 kN/m) facing

boq_items.description: Installation of sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains (Ø75mm, Schedule 80) at 5°–10° upward rake into hillside with cleanout cap. (5 Nos. × 15m)
boq_items.short_description: Slotted PVC sub-horizontal relief drains (Ø75mm) at 5°–10° rake (5 Nos. × 15m)

boq_items.description: Construction of lined stone masonry saucer catch drain (0.60m × 0.60m) along slope crest to intercept surface runoff.
boq_items.short_description: Stone masonry saucer catch drain (0.60×0.60m) along slope crest in 1:4 mortar

boq_items.description: Reconstruction of damaged roadside longitudinal rectangular drain (0.60m × 0.60m) in stone masonry with M15 concrete bedding.
boq_items.short_description: Reconstruction of roadside longitudinal drain (0.60×0.60m) in stone masonry

boq_items.description: Stepped cascade stone-pitched drainage chute down slope flank to safely discharge crest drain runoff into road culvert.
boq_items.short_description: Stepped cascade stone-pitched drainage chute down slope flank into ravine

boq_items.description: Soil bioengineering: 700 GSM coir netting, hydroseeding with native grass mixes, and Vetiver grass contour slips across upper cut face. (108.96 m² + 10% overlap)
boq_items.short_description: Coir geotextile netting (700 GSM), hydroseeding & Vetiver grass contour hedges

plain_language_explanation.summary_title: Moderate Landslide & Dwelling Impact in Mandi Sector
plain_language_explanation.what_happened: A steep section of the hillside gave way, sending wet mud, soil, and debris crashing directly into the back and side of a residential house.
plain_language_explanation.why_it_happened: Prolonged rainfall saturated the unreinforced slope above the home, causing the top layer of earth to lose friction and slide down under its own weight.
plain_language_explanation.property_and_access_impact: The house has suffered severe structural damage with mud breaching interior rooms. The building is unsafe and residents must stay outside.
plain_language_explanation.road_and_travel_impact: The house has suffered severe structural damage with mud breaching interior rooms. The building is unsafe and residents must stay outside.
plain_language_explanation.ongoing_hazards: The hillside above is still wet and vulnerable. Any more rainfall could cause another mudslide and total collapse of the damaged structure.
plain_language_explanation.what_needs_to_be_done: Turn off power and water to the house, carefully clear out 165 m³ of mud, and construct a concrete retaining wall with drainage behind the house to stop future slides.
plain_language_explanation.citizen_safety_advice: Do NOT enter the damaged house. Keep all onlookers and family members at least 30 meters away from the wet hill face.

tier_1_factual_evidence.title: Tier 1: Factual Ground Truth & Telemetry (Objective Past Passive)
tier_1_factual_evidence.description: At Kangra Sector — Hill Road Corridor (Kangra Sector), a detachment scarp of vertical height 6.40 m (upper face 3.60 m inclined at 66°) was surveyed. Saturated upper siwalik soft sandstone, siltstone and boulder conglomerate debris (48.0 m³ in-situ / 60.00 m³ bulked calculated via Simpson's prismoidal rule at 1.25 bulking factor) encroached 0.00 m across the 0.00 m carriageway formation. Roadside drainage was 100% obstructed under active hydrostatic surcharge. Prior to failure, the cut slope was an unprotected excavation. Discontinuities dipping 42° adversely into the slope face were measured with aperture 15–40 mm.
tier_1_factual_evidence.weathering_grade: Grade IV to V (Highly to Completely Weathered)

tier_2_analytical_mechanics.title: Tier 2: Analytical Geotechnical Mechanics & FoS (Calibrated Engineering Inferences)
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.description: Under the Cruden & Varnes (1996) and USGS Circular 1325 classification, the failure is designated as a Debris Slump / Mudslide Mass Movement (Cruden & Varnes, 1996) within Upper Siwalik Soft Sandstone, Siltstone and Boulder Conglomerate strata. Under dry baseline conditions, limit equilibrium stability analysis (Hoek & Bray planar cleft-water mechanics) yields FoS = 1.34 (marginal). During monsoon steady-seepage saturation with active joint cleft-water hydrostatic pressure (zw = 1.2m), calculated FoS drops to 0.87, confirming active shear mobilization along daylighting joint set J1 (slip plane inclined length L_slip = 6.856 m). Following multi-barrier stabilization, post-remediation FoS is verified at 1.85. The site lies in Seismic Zone V (Z = 0.36, ah = 0.09g).
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.disclaimer: Subsurface geotechnical parameters (effective cohesion c' = 14.0 kPa, effective internal friction angle φ' = 28.0°, intact rock UCS = 35.0 MPa, and structural joint dip = 57.0°) are preliminary model estimates and assumptions based on empirical rock mass classifications and regional lithological analogs. These values are strictly subject to confirmatory site investigation, trial-pit logging, and rotary borehole core extraction with laboratory testing prior to detailed engineering design, statutory tendering, or construction authorization.

tier_3_statutory_directives.title: Tier 3: Statutory Remediation Directives & Civil Schedule (Imperative Standards)
tier_3_statutory_directives.description:
1. Construct a 15m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H_stem=2.80m, D_f=0.90m, Base B=1.65m, Top b=0.30m, volume = 20.70 m³ M15 with 40% plums per IS:14458 Part 2), backed by 11.25 m³ filter pack and 20 Nos. weep holes.
2. Install 18 Nos. Ø25mm High-Yield Fe500D soil nails (16 working in 1.8m H × 2.0m V grid + 2 sacrificial pullout verification test nails) drilled to 9.0m depth (180m drill, 190m bar, 18 pads, 91.12 m² wire mesh) per MoRTH Section 3100.
3. Install 5 Nos. × 15m (75.0m total) sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains (Ø75mm, Schedule 80) at 5°–10° upward rake, paired with 25.0m crest saucer catch drain (0.60m × 0.60m), 17.0m roadside drain (0.60m × 0.60m), and 22.0m stepped cascade chute per MoRTH Section 300.
4. Lay 700 GSM coir geotextile netting (66.00 m² with 10% overlap), hydroseeding, and Vetiver grass contour hedges per MoRTH Section 1802.

usgs_classification.usgs_general_definition: A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement.
usgs_classification.usgs_kinematic_definition: A downslope movement of rock or soil, or both, occurring on the surface of rupture—either curved (rotational slide) or planar (translational slide) rupture—in which much of the material often moves as a coherent or semicoherent mass with little internal deformation.
usgs_classification.material_definition: Soil containing a significant proportion of coarse fragments; 20% to 80% of the particles are greater than 2 mm in size (gravel, cobbles, and boulders).
usgs_classification.movement_definition: A slide in which the surface of rupture is curved concavely upward (spoon-shaped) and the slide movement is roughly rotational about an axis parallel to the ground surface.

landslide_anatomy.crown_and_scarp: Undisplaced crown with open extensional crown cracks; distinct steep main scarp exposing rupture surface.
landslide_anatomy.displaced_mass: Depleted mass above planar/rotational surface of rupture, extending downslope into zone of accumulation.
landslide_anatomy.toe_and_foot: Displaced foot advancing beyond toe of rupture surface across roadway/property margin.

geological: Weak, weathered, or fractured rock and soil materials
Adversely oriented structural discontinuities (faults, joints, bedding planes daylighting into cut face)
morphological: Fluvial or wave erosion undermining the slope toe

physical_trigger: Prolonged antecedent precipitation and high-intensity storm rainfall
Transient perched groundwater table development and loss of matric suction
human_causes: Anthropogenic excavation / toe undercutting for roadway benching or foundation cuts
Surcharge loading at the slope crest (unengineered spoil disposal or building construction)

boq_items.short_description: Free-draining graded granular filter backfill behind RC wall

boq_items.description: Providing and laying 100mm dia perforated PVC weep hole pipes laid at 1:20 slope through RC stem with geotextile covers. (26 holes × 0.60m)
boq_items.short_description: 100mm dia perforated PVC weep hole pipes through RC wall stem

boq_items.description: Rotary drilling of Ø76mm boreholes using portable lightweight tripod rig on upper residential terrace. (22 working + 2 sacrificial = 24 holes × 6.0m)
boq_items.short_description: Rotary drilling of Ø76mm dowel holes with tripod rig (24 Nos. × 6.0m)

boq_items.description: Supplying and inserting Ø25mm Fe500D TMT soil dowel bars with centralizers in upper terrace boreholes. (24 bars × 6.5m)
boq_items.short_description: Ø25mm Fe500D TMT soil dowel bars on residential terrace (24 Nos.)

boq_items.description: Pressure grouting of dowel boreholes with non-shrink cement mortar (fcu ≥ 30 MPa, W/C = 0.42). (24 holes × 6.0m)
boq_items.short_description: Pressure grouting of dowel boreholes with non-shrink cement mortar

boq_items.description: Construction of lined peripheral trapezoidal garland cutoff drain (0.50m × 0.50m) in cement concrete M15 around upper residential terrace boundary.
boq_items.short_description: Lined trapezoidal garland cutoff drain (0.50×0.50m) in M15 concrete

boq_items.description: Stepped masonry drainage disposal chute discharging upper terrace runoff safely into natural municipal ravine.
boq_items.short_description: Stepped masonry drainage disposal chute into natural drainage ravine

boq_items.description: Soil bioengineering: 700 GSM coir netting, hydroseeding with native grass mixes, and Vetiver grass contour slips across terrace cut slope.
boq_items.short_description: Coir netting (700 GSM) & Vetiver grass contour slips across cut slope

cedd_assessment.consequence_criteria: Residential dwellings, schools, hospitals, commercial complexes, or heavily trafficked National Highway corridors where failure poses immediate threat to human life.

inspection_regime.name: Detailed Stability Assessment
inspection_regime.frequency: Immediate upon occurrence of major slope failure (>50 m³ displaced volume) or active tension cracking (>10mm aperture)
inspection_regime.personnel: Senior Geotechnical Engineering Specialist / Academic Panel
inspection_regime.key_checks: Subsurface core drilling, limit equilibrium back-analysis (Bishop / Morgenstern-Price), kinematic rock joint stereonet audit

primary_structural.name: Passive Grouted Soil Nailing Array (CEDD Geoguide 7 Standard)
primary_structural.description: Closely spaced grid (1.5-2.0m) of high-yield steel bars (25-32mm) fully grouted into pre-drilled boreholes with RC head pads.

hydrogeological_drainage.name: Sub-Horizontal Directional Relief Drains (GEO Standard)
hydrogeological_drainage.description: Array of perforated PVC pipes (50-75mm dia, 15-30m length) drilled at 5-10 deg upward rake into slope to depress water table.

nature_based_solution.name: Live Vegetated Crib Wall / Timber Cribbing
nature_based_solution.description: Hollow box-like interlocking timber or precast concrete beam framework backfilled with soil/rock and planted with live root cuttings.

usgs_classification.usgs_general_definition: A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement.
usgs_classification.usgs_kinematic_definition: A downslope movement of rock or soil, or both, occurring on the surface of rupture—either curved (rotational slide) or planar (translational slide) rupture—in which much of the material often moves as a coherent or semicoherent mass with little internal deformation.
usgs_classification.material_definition: Soil containing a significant proportion of coarse fragments; 20% to 80% of the particles are greater than 2 mm in size (gravel, cobbles, and boulders).
usgs_classification.movement_definition: A slide in which the surface of rupture is curved concavely upward (spoon-shaped) and the slide movement is roughly rotational about an axis parallel to the ground surface.

velocity_class.consequences: Escape possible; property and structures destroyed; roads severely disrupted.

landslide_anatomy.crown_and_scarp: Undisplaced crown with open extensional crown cracks; distinct steep main scarp exposing rupture surface.
landslide_anatomy.displaced_mass: Depleted mass above planar/rotational surface of rupture, extending downslope into zone of accumulation.
landslide_anatomy.toe_and_foot: Displaced foot advancing beyond toe of rupture surface across roadway/property margin.

geological: Weak, weathered, or fractured rock and soil materials
Adversely oriented structural discontinuities (faults, joints, bedding planes daylighting into cut face)
morphological: Fluvial or wave erosion undermining the slope toe
Tectonic or steep gravitational escarpment oversteepening
physical_trigger: Prolonged antecedent precipitation and high-intensity storm rainfall
Transient perched groundwater table development and loss of matric suction
human_causes: Anthropogenic excavation / toe undercutting for roadway benching or foundation cuts
Surcharge loading at the slope crest (unengineered spoil disposal or building construction)

usgs_classification.standard_reference: USGS Circular 1325 (Highland & Bobrowsky, 2008) & Cruden & Varnes (1996) TRB Special Report 247

bhukosh_geology.primary_rock: Shali Dolomite & Sundernagar Quartzite with interbedded phyllitic slate
bhukosh_geology.structure: Joints dipping 50°–65° adversely daylighting into road cut
bhukosh_geology.citation: Geological Survey of India (GSI) Stratigraphic Atlas of Himachal Pradesh

IITM-CR-B0B0D035.mitigation_measures:
1. Primary Toe Retention & Arrest (LaRiMiT Cluster 4 / IS:14458 / CEDD Geoguide 1):
   Emergency hydraulic clearance of 200 m³ displaced debris followed by construction of a 18m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H=2.6m, Base=1.30m, Embedment=1.00m) with 100mm dia PVC weep holes @ 1.20m c/c staggered in non-woven geotextile envelopes.
2. Internal Ground Reinforcement (LaRiMiT Cluster 5 / CEDD Geoguide 7):
   Prescribed Soil Nailing Array (Dia. 25 mm (Fe500 High-Yield Deformed Steel)) installed in 100 mm drillholes at 15° to 20° downward rake, 2.00 m (H) x 2.00 m (V) Staggered Pattern, length 8.0 m to 12.0 m, neat cementitious grout (f_cu >= 30 MPa) with 2% sacrificial pullout verification testing.
3. Hydrogeological Pore-Pressure Depression (LaRiMiT Cluster 3 / CEDD TGN 24):
   Subsurface Directional Drainage Array: 15.0 m per borehole (Total 5 Nos. array) slotted PVC pipes (O90 geotextile filter sock) installed at 5° to 10° upward rake for gravity self-cleansing flow to discharge perched groundwater, supplemented by lined crest interceptor catch drains (0.68 m x 0.45 m) and hillside saucer channels.
4. Dynamic Rockfall / Debris Barrier (LaRiMiT Cluster 6 / CEDD GEO Report 138):
   Installation of 500 kJ Rating flexible ring net barrier (H=3.0 m, HEB 140 Structural Steel Section) with energy dissipators along active fall chutes.
5. Nature-Based Solutions & Bioengineering (LaRiMiT Cluster 8):
   Live Vegetated Crib Wall / Timber Cribbing and coir geotextile bio-turfing (700 GSM) across reprofiled slope faces to restore matric suction and prevent shallow surficial raveling.
IITM-CR-B0B0D035.other_observations: Sub-surface groundwater seepage daylighting along the colluvial mantle and Phyllite bedrock interface, confirming elevated perched phreatic levels during rainfall. Active extensional tension fissures (apertures 15-45 mm) trace 8-15 m uphill of the detachment crown. Relict discontinuity set J1 (44° dip daylighting adversely into the slope face) exhibits planar persistent slickensides with iron-oxide staining, confirming kinematic daylighting and high susceptibility to progressive retrogressive failure during prolonged monsoon precipitation.

IITM-CR-B0B0D035.synthesis_remarks:
1. GEOTECHNICAL & USGS CLASSIFICATION (USGS Circular 1325 / Cruden & Varnes 1996):
Forensic field reconnaissance of the Mandi sector confirms an active mass wasting event conforming strictly to the USGS standard definition of a landslide: "A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement."
Under the Cruden & Varnes (1996) two-term taxonomy, the failure is formally designated as: Translational Rock Slide (Rock Block Slide) (Kinematic Movement: Translational Slide, Substrate: Rock, Velocity Rating: Rapid [Class 5, 1.8 m/h to 3 m/min]).

2. CONSEQUENCE RATING & TARGET FACTOR OF SAFETY (CEDD Geoguide 1):
Directly impacting mandi sub-divisional hill road corridor. Under Hong Kong CEDD Geoguide 1 criteria, the slope is classified as Category 3 (Low Consequence), requiring a statutory minimum target Factor of Safety FOS >= 1.15 under 10-year return period rainfall (FOS >= 1.05 under extreme storm conditions).

3. KINEMATIC FAILURE MECHANICS, ANATOMY & HYDROGEOLOGY:
Instability is characterized by A landslide mass that moves out, or down and outward, along a relatively planar surface with little rotational movement or backward tilting; frequently controlled by structural discontinuities (bedding, joints, faults). within Phyllite strata under steep cut geometry (63° to 67° (Unstable Hill Cut Face)). Diagnostic landslide anatomical features (USGS Circular 1325) include an exposed detachment main scarp and depletion mass, open tension crown fissures, and an accumulation toe encroaching upon the corridor. Failure was triggered by antecedent rainfall infiltration inducing transient perched groundwater tables, loss of matric suction in the upper colluvium, and hydrostatic cleft-water pressure along daylighting relict joints (dipping 44° into the cut face).

4. MULTI-BARRIER MITIGATION STRATEGY (LaRiMiT / CEDD GEO Standards):
- Primary Toe Retention (LaRiMiT Cluster 4): Construction of a 18m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H=2.6m, Base B=1.30m) founded on competent bedrock with 100mm PVC weep holes @ 1.2m c/c.
- Internal Ground Reinforcement (LaRiMiT Cluster 5 / CEDD Geoguide 7): Prescribed Soil Nailing Array (Dia. 25 mm (Fe500 High-Yield Deformed Steel), 2.00 m (H) x 2.00 m (V) Staggered Pattern, length 8.0 m to 12.0 m) with sacrificial pullout verification testing.
- Pore Pressure Relief (LaRiMiT Cluster 3 / CEDD TGN 24): Installation of 15.0 m per borehole (Total 5 Nos. array) sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains inclined at 5° to 10° upward rake for gravity self-cleansing flow to intercept perched seepage, paired with lined crest interceptor drains (0.68 m x 0.45 m).
- Dynamic Impact & NBS Protection: 500 kJ Rating flexible ring net barrier (CEDD GEO Report No. 138 / EOTA EAD 340059-00-0106) in fall zones, combined with Live Vegetated Crib Wall / Timber Cribbing.

5. STATUTORY MAINTENANCE REGIME:
Mandatory Routine Maintenance Inspection (RMI) at Monthly during monsoon season (June–September) and quarterly in dry season by a Junior Field Staff / Highway Section Observer in strict accordance with CEDD Geoguide 5.

plain_language_explanation.summary_title: Moderate Landslide & Corridor Disruption in Mandi Sector
plain_language_explanation.what_happened: A steep section of the hillside gave way, dumping loose phyllite and boulders across the corridor.
plain_language_explanation.why_it_happened: Heavy rainfall soaked deep into the mountain slope, lubricating natural slip planes until the slope gave way.
plain_language_explanation.property_and_access_impact: Passage is obstructed (2.55 m (Single-Lane Restricted / Shoulder Lost)). Vehicles and pedestrians cannot safely transit this point.
plain_language_explanation.road_and_travel_impact: Passage is obstructed (2.55 m (Single-Lane Restricted / Shoulder Lost)). Vehicles and pedestrians cannot safely transit this point.
plain_language_explanation.ongoing_hazards: The hillside directly above remains unstable. Any additional rain, wind, or ground vibration can dislodge more loose rocks.
plain_language_explanation.what_needs_to_be_done: Deploy heavy excavators to clear 200 m³ of boulders and build a 2.6m retaining wall at the slope toe.
plain_language_explanation.citizen_safety_advice: Do NOT attempt to cross under the fallen slope. Maintain a safe distance of at least 50 meters.

tier_1_factual_evidence.title: Tier 1: Factual Ground Truth & Telemetry (Objective Past Passive)
tier_1_factual_evidence.description: At Mandi Sector — Hill Road Corridor (Mandi Sector), a detachment scarp of vertical height 7.60 m (upper face 4.90 m inclined at 66°) was surveyed. Saturated shali dolomite & sundernagar quartzite with interbedded phyllitic slate / dharamsala sandstone debris (145.0 m³ in-situ / 181.25 m³ bulked calculated via Simpson's prismoidal rule at 1.25 bulking factor) encroached 2.95 m across the 5.25 m carriageway formation. Roadside drainage was 100% obstructed under active hydrostatic surcharge. Prior to failure, the cut slope was an unprotected excavation. Discontinuities dipping 57° adversely into the slope face were measured with aperture 15–40 mm.

tier_2_analytical_mechanics.title: Tier 2: Analytical Geotechnical Mechanics & FoS (Calibrated Engineering Inferences)
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.description: Under the Cruden & Varnes (1996) and USGS Circular 1325 classification, the failure is designated as a Translational Debris Slide Mass Movement (Cruden & Varnes, 1996) within Shali Dolomite & Sundernagar Quartzite with interbedded phyllitic slate / Dharamsala Sandstone strata. Under dry baseline conditions, limit equilibrium stability analysis (Hoek & Bray planar cleft-water mechanics) yields FoS = 1.01 (marginal). During monsoon steady-seepage saturation with active joint cleft-water hydrostatic pressure (zw = 1.2m), calculated FoS drops to 0.60, confirming active shear mobilization along daylighting joint set J1 (slip plane inclined length L_slip = 6.856 m). Following multi-barrier stabilization, post-remediation FoS is verified at 1.54. The site lies in Seismic Zone V (Z = 0.36, ah = 0.09g).
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.disclaimer: Subsurface geotechnical parameters (effective cohesion c' = 14.0 kPa, effective internal friction angle φ' = 28.0°, intact rock UCS = 35.0 MPa, and structural joint dip = 57.0°) are preliminary model estimates and assumptions based on empirical rock mass classifications and regional lithological analogs. These values are strictly subject to confirmatory site investigation, trial-pit logging, and rotary borehole core extraction with laboratory testing prior to detailed engineering design, statutory tendering, or construction authorization.

tier_3_statutory_directives.title: Tier 3: Statutory Remediation Directives & Civil Schedule (Imperative Standards)
tier_3_statutory_directives.description:
1. Construct a 17m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H_stem=2.70m, D_f=1.00m, Base B=1.35m, Top b=0.60m, volume = 67.70 m³ M15 with 40% plums per IS:14458 Part 2), backed by 16.07 m³ filter pack and 26 Nos. weep holes.
2. Install 20 Nos. Ø25mm High-Yield Fe500D soil nails (18 working in 1.8m H × 2.0m V grid + 2 sacrificial pullout verification test nails) drilled to 9.0m depth (180m drill, 190m bar, 18 pads, 91.12 m² wire mesh) per MoRTH Section 3100.
3. Install 5 Nos. × 15m (75.0m total) sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains (Ø75mm, Schedule 80) at 5°–10° upward rake, paired with 25.0m crest saucer catch drain (0.60m × 0.60m), 17.0m roadside drain (0.60m × 0.60m), and 22.0m stepped cascade chute per MoRTH Section 300.
4. Lay 700 GSM coir geotextile netting (100.23 m² with 10% overlap), hydroseeding, and Vetiver grass contour hedges per MoRTH Section 1802.

usgs_classification.usgs_general_definition: A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement.
usgs_classification.usgs_kinematic_definition: A downslope movement of rock or soil, or both, occurring on the surface of rupture—either curved (rotational slide) or planar (translational slide) rupture—in which much of the material often moves as a coherent or semicoherent mass with little internal deformation.
usgs_classification.material_definition: Soil containing a significant proportion of coarse fragments; 20% to 80% of the particles are greater than 2 mm in size (gravel, cobbles, and boulders).
usgs_classification.movement_definition: A landslide mass that moves out, or down and outward, along a relatively planar surface with little rotational movement or backward tilting; frequently controlled by structural discontinuities (bedding, joints, faults).

velocity_class.consequences: Escape possible; property and structures destroyed; roads severely disrupted.

landslide_anatomy.crown_and_scarp: Undisplaced crown with open extensional crown cracks; distinct steep main scarp exposing rupture surface.
landslide_anatomy.displaced_mass: Depleted mass above planar/rotational surface of rupture, extending downslope into zone of accumulation.
landslide_anatomy.toe_and_foot: Displaced foot advancing beyond toe of rupture surface across roadway/property margin.

geological: Weak, weathered, or fractured rock and soil materials
Adversely oriented structural discontinuities (faults, joints, bedding planes daylighting into cut face)
morphological: Fluvial or wave erosion undermining the slope toe
Tectonic or steep gravitational escarpment oversteepening
physical_trigger: Prolonged antecedent precipitation and high-intensity storm rainfall
Transient perched groundwater table development and loss of matric suction
human_causes: Anthropogenic excavation / toe undercutting for roadway benching or foundation cuts
Surcharge loading at the slope crest (unengineered spoil disposal or building construction)

usgs_classification.standard_reference: USGS Circular 1325 (Highland & Bobrowsky, 2008) & Cruden & Varnes (1996) TRB Special Report 247

IITM-CR-6A9B327E.mitigation_measures:
1. Primary Toe Retention & Structural Retention (IS:14458 Part 2 / MoRTH Section 1500):
   Emergency hydraulic clearance of 181.25 m³ bulked debris (145.0 m³ in-situ @ 1.25 bulking) followed by construction of a 17.0m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H_stem = 2.70m, D_f = 1.00m embedment, base width B = 1.35m, top width b = 0.60m, concrete volume = 67.70 m³ M15 with 40% plums 150–300mm), backed by 16.07 m³ crushed gravel filter pack (0.35m thick) wrapped in 67.25 m² non-woven geotextile and 26 Nos. 100mm dia PVC weep hole pipes (32.50m total) in 2 staggered rows.
2. Internal Ground Reinforcement & Slope Nailing (MoRTH Section 3100 / CEDD Geoguide 7):
   Installation of 20 Nos. Ø25mm High-Yield Fe500D TMT soil nails (18 working nails in 1.8m H × 2.0m V staggered grid + 2 sacrificial pullout verification test nails) drilled to 9.0m depth (180.0m total drilling, 190.0m bar), pressure grouted with non-shrink cementitious grout (fcu ≥ 30 MPa), anchored with 18 Nos. cast-in-situ M30 RC bearing pads (400×400×200mm) and high-tensile diamond steel wire mesh facing (3mm wire, 65×65mm, 91.12 m²).
3. Hydrogeological Pore-Pressure Relief & Surface Drainage (MoRTH Section 300, Clause 309 / IRC:SP:48):
   Installation of 5 Nos. × 15m (75.0m total) sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains (Ø75mm, Schedule 80) drilled at 5°–10° upward rake into the hillside to depress perched cleft-water tables, accompanied by 25.0m stone masonry saucer catch drain (0.60m × 0.60m) along slope crest, 17.0m reconstructed roadside longitudinal drain (0.60m × 0.60m), and 22.0m stepped cascade stone-pitched chute.
4. Soil Bioengineering & Surficial Erosion Control (MoRTH Section 1802 / IS:14458):
   Dressing and reprofiling upper cut face (91.12 m²), laying 700 GSM biodegradable coir geotextile netting with 10% overlap (100.23 m²), hydraulic hydroseeding with native mountain grass seeds, and planting deep-rooting Vetiver grass (Chrysopogon zizanioides) contour hedges.
IITM-CR-6A9B327E.other_observations: Sub-surface groundwater seepage daylighting along the colluvial mantle and bedrock interface, confirming elevated perched phreatic levels during rainfall. Active extensional tension fissures (apertures 15-40 mm) trace uphill of the detachment crown. Relict discontinuity set J1 (57° dip daylighting adversely into the slope face) exhibits planar persistent slickensides with iron-oxide staining, confirming kinematic daylighting and high susceptibility to progressive retrogressive failure during prolonged monsoon precipitation.

IITM-CR-6A9B327E.synthesis_remarks:
1. GEOTECHNICAL & KINEMATIC CLASSIFICATION (USGS Circular 1325 / Cruden & Varnes 1996):
Forensic geotechnical evaluation of the Mandi Sector MDR corridor (RD 17+432, 31.70800° N, 76.93200° E) confirms an active slope failure formally designated under Cruden & Varnes (1996) taxonomy as a Composite Translational Debris-Rock Slide. The failure detachment occurred along daylighting structural joint set J1 dipping 57° SW in Grade IV highly weathered Shali Dolomite / Quartzite bedrock, releasing 145.0 m³ in-situ (181.25 m³ bulked @ 1.25 swell) of colluvial overburden and boulder debris across the carriageway, restricting the 5.25m formation to 2.30m single-lane transit.

2. CONSEQUENCE RATING & LIMIT STATE STABILITY (CEDD Geoguide 1 / Eurocode 7):
Under Hong Kong CEDD Geoguide 1 consequence classification, this corridor represents Category 2 (High / Sub-Divisional Corridor Life & Transport Consequence), requiring a statutory minimum Factor of Safety FoS ≥ 1.30 under extreme monsoon steady-seepage saturation and FoS ≥ 1.50 under long-term permanent stabilized conditions. Prior to failure, the unprotected cut slope had an estimated dry baseline FoS of 1.48, which collapsed to FoS = 0.92 under monsoon joint cleft-water hydrostatic saturation (zw = 1.2m), causing catastrophic shear detachment along the 6.856m inclined failure surface.

3. MULTI-BARRIER MITIGATION STRATEGY (IS:14458 / MoRTH Section 3100 / CEDD Geoguide 7):
- Primary Toe Retention: Construction of a 17.0m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H_stem = 2.70m, D_f = 1.00m, base width B = 1.35m, top width b = 0.60m, concrete volume = 67.70 m³ M15 with 40% plums per IS:14458 Part 2) with 16.07 m³ granular filter pack and 26 Nos. 100mm PVC weep holes.
- Internal Ground Reinforcement: Prescribed Soil Nailing Array (Ø25mm Fe500D TMT rebar, 20 Nos. @ 9.0m depth, 180m drilling, 1.8m H × 2.0m V grid) with 18 Nos. M30 RC bearing pads (400×400×200mm), high-tensile diamond steel wire mesh (91.12 m²), and 2 sacrificial pullout proof verification tests (MoRTH 3100).

Direct physical asset restoration (₹ 3,02,262.50 under SDRF Section 48(1)(a)) and indirect freight detour disruption (₹ 1,25,000.00) are strictly segregated from contractor procurement.

plain_language_explanation.summary_title: MDR Corridor Landslide Disruption in Mandi Sector (RD 17+432)
plain_language_explanation.what_happened: A steep section of the hillside cut scarp failed, dumping 181 m³ of colluvial debris and boulders across the road corridor.
plain_language_explanation.why_it_happened: Heavy monsoon rainfall saturated open joint discontinuities dipping 57° into the roadway, inducing hydrostatic cleft-water pressure and shear collapse.
plain_language_explanation.property_and_access_impact: Passage is obstructed (2.95 m (Single-Lane Restricted / Shoulder Lost: 2.30m Operable)). Two-way traffic is halted; single-lane transit is restricted under safety spotters.

plain_language_explanation.ongoing_hazards: The hillside directly above remains vulnerable to secondary detachment under continuous precipitation.
plain_language_explanation.what_needs_to_be_done: Deploy excavators to clear 181 m³ of debris, construct a 17m plum concrete breast wall (H=2.7m), install 20 soil nails, and drill 75m of subsurface drainage.

tier_1_factual_evidence.title: Tier 1: Factual Ground Truth & Telemetry (Objective Past Passive)
tier_1_factual_evidence.description: At Mandi Sector — Major District Road (MDR), Chainage RD 17+432 (Km 17/432) (RD 17+432 (Km 17/432)), a detachment scarp of vertical height 7.60 m (upper face 4.90 m inclined at 66°) was surveyed. Saturated shali dolomite & sundernagar quartzite with interbedded phyllite clasts debris (145.0 m³ in-situ / 181.25 m³ bulked calculated via Simpson's prismoidal rule at 1.25 bulking factor) encroached 2.95 m across the 5.25 m carriageway formation. Roadside drainage was 100% obstructed under active hydrostatic surcharge. Prior to failure, the cut slope was an unprotected excavation. Discontinuities dipping 57° adversely into the slope face were measured with aperture 15–40 mm.

tier_2_analytical_mechanics.title: Tier 2: Analytical Geotechnical Mechanics & FoS (Calibrated Engineering Inferences)
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.description: Under the Cruden & Varnes (1996) and USGS Circular 1325 classification, the failure is designated as a Composite Translational Debris-Rock Slide (Cruden & Varnes, 1996) within Shali Dolomite & Sundernagar Quartzite with interbedded phyllite clasts strata. Under dry baseline conditions, limit equilibrium stability analysis (Hoek & Bray planar cleft-water mechanics) yields FoS = 1.01 (marginal). During monsoon steady-seepage saturation with active joint cleft-water hydrostatic pressure (zw = 1.2m), calculated FoS drops to 0.60, confirming active shear mobilization along daylighting joint set J1 (slip plane inclined length L_slip = 6.856 m). Following multi-barrier stabilization, post-remediation FoS is verified at 1.54. The site lies in Seismic Zone V (Z = 0.36, ah = 0.09g).
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.disclaimer: Subsurface geotechnical parameters (effective cohesion c' = 14.0 kPa, effective internal friction angle φ' = 28.0°, intact rock UCS = 35.0 MPa, and structural joint dip = 57.0°) are preliminary model estimates and assumptions based on empirical rock mass classifications and regional lithological analogs. These values are strictly subject to confirmatory site investigation, trial-pit logging, and rotary borehole core extraction with laboratory testing prior to detailed engineering design, statutory tendering, or construction authorization.

tier_3_statutory_directives.title: Tier 3: Statutory Remediation Directives & Civil Schedule (Imperative Standards)
tier_3_statutory_directives.description:
1. Construct a 17m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H_stem=2.70m, D_f=1.00m, Base B=1.35m, Top b=0.60m, volume = 67.70 m³ M15 with 40% plums per IS:14458 Part 2), backed by 16.07 m³ filter pack and 26 Nos. weep holes.
2. Install 20 Nos. Ø25mm High-Yield Fe500D soil nails (18 working in 1.8m H × 2.0m V grid + 2 sacrificial pullout verification test nails) drilled to 9.0m depth (180m drill, 190m bar, 18 pads, 91.12 m² wire mesh) per MoRTH Section 3100.
3. Install 5 Nos. × 15m (75.0m total) sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains (Ø75mm, Schedule 80) at 5°–10° upward rake, paired with 25.0m crest saucer catch drain (0.60m × 0.60m), 17.0m roadside drain (0.60m × 0.60m), and 22.0m stepped cascade chute per MoRTH Section 300.
4. Lay 700 GSM coir geotextile netting (100.23 m² with 10% overlap), hydroseeding, and Vetiver grass contour hedges per MoRTH Section 1802.

usgs_classification.usgs_general_definition: A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement.
usgs_classification.usgs_kinematic_definition: A downslope movement of rock or soil, or both, occurring on the surface of rupture—either curved (rotational slide) or planar (translational slide) rupture—in which much of the material often moves as a coherent or semicoherent mass with little internal deformation.
usgs_classification.material_definition: Soil containing a significant proportion of coarse fragments; 20% to 80% of the particles are greater than 2 mm in size (gravel, cobbles, and boulders).
usgs_classification.movement_definition: A landslide mass that moves out, or down and outward, along a relatively planar surface with little rotational movement or backward tilting; frequently controlled by structural discontinuities (bedding, joints, faults).

velocity_class.consequences: Escape possible; property and structures destroyed; roads severely disrupted.

landslide_anatomy.crown_and_scarp: Undisplaced crown with open extensional crown cracks; distinct steep main scarp exposing rupture surface.
landslide_anatomy.displaced_mass: Depleted mass above planar/rotational surface of rupture, extending downslope into zone of accumulation.
landslide_anatomy.toe_and_foot: Displaced foot advancing beyond toe of rupture surface across roadway/property margin.

geological: Weak, weathered, or fractured rock and soil materials
Adversely oriented structural discontinuities (faults, joints, bedding planes daylighting into cut face)
morphological: Fluvial or wave erosion undermining the slope toe
Tectonic or steep gravitational escarpment oversteepening
physical_trigger: Prolonged antecedent precipitation and high-intensity storm rainfall
Transient perched groundwater table development and loss of matric suction
human_causes: Anthropogenic excavation / toe undercutting for roadway benching or foundation cuts
Surcharge loading at the slope crest (unengineered spoil disposal or building construction)

usgs_classification.usgs_general_definition: A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement.
usgs_classification.usgs_kinematic_definition: A downslope movement of rock or soil, or both, occurring on the surface of rupture—either curved (rotational slide) or planar (translational slide) rupture—in which much of the material often moves as a coherent or semicoherent mass with little internal deformation.
usgs_classification.material_definition: Soil containing a significant proportion of coarse fragments; 20% to 80% of the particles are greater than 2 mm in size (gravel, cobbles, and boulders).
usgs_classification.movement_definition: A landslide mass that moves out, or down and outward, along a relatively planar surface with little rotational movement or backward tilting; frequently controlled by structural discontinuities (bedding, joints, faults).

velocity_class.consequences: Escape possible; property and structures destroyed; roads severely disrupted.

landslide_anatomy.crown_and_scarp: Undisplaced crown with open extensional crown cracks; distinct steep main scarp exposing rupture surface.
landslide_anatomy.displaced_mass: Depleted mass above planar/rotational surface of rupture, extending downslope into zone of accumulation.
landslide_anatomy.toe_and_foot: Displaced foot advancing beyond toe of rupture surface across roadway/property margin.

geological: Weak, weathered, or fractured rock and soil materials
Adversely oriented structural discontinuities (faults, joints, bedding planes daylighting into cut face)
morphological: Fluvial or wave erosion undermining the slope toe
Tectonic or steep gravitational escarpment oversteepening
physical_trigger: Prolonged antecedent precipitation and high-intensity storm rainfall
Transient perched groundwater table development and loss of matric suction
human_causes: Anthropogenic excavation / toe undercutting for roadway benching or foundation cuts
Surcharge loading at the slope crest (unengineered spoil disposal or building construction)

usgs_classification.standard_reference: USGS Circular 1325 (Highland & Bobrowsky, 2008) & Cruden & Varnes (1996) TRB Special Report 247

1. GEOTECHNICAL CLASSIFICATION: Rotational subsidence and outer roadway embankment slip-out along valley-side shoulder.
2. PRIMARY RETENTION DESIGN: Construction of stepped PVC-coated wire gabion gravity retaining wall (H=4.5m, Base=2.93m) founded on competent valley bedrock bench with non-woven geotextile backing.

5. HYDROLOGY: Perforated HDPE subsoil collector drain to prevent valley embankment pore pressure buildup.

tier_1_factual_evidence.title: Tier 1: Factual Ground Truth & Telemetry (Objective Past Passive)
tier_1_factual_evidence.description: At Mandi Sector — Hill Road Corridor (Mandi Sector), a detachment scarp of vertical height 7.50 m (upper face 3.00 m inclined at 66°) was surveyed. Saturated shali dolomite & sundernagar quartzite with interbedded phyllitic slate / dharamsala sandstone debris (59.4 m³ in-situ / 74.25 m³ bulked calculated via Simpson's prismoidal rule at 1.25 bulking factor) encroached 3.40 m across the 5.50 m carriageway formation. Roadside drainage was 100% obstructed under active hydrostatic surcharge. Prior to failure, the cut slope was an unprotected excavation. Discontinuities dipping 38° adversely into the slope face were measured with aperture 15–40 mm.

tier_2_analytical_mechanics.title: Tier 2: Analytical Geotechnical Mechanics & FoS (Calibrated Engineering Inferences)
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.description: Under the Cruden & Varnes (1996) and USGS Circular 1325 classification, the failure is designated as a Subsidence / Embankment Slump Mass Movement (Cruden & Varnes, 1996) within Shali Dolomite & Sundernagar Quartzite with interbedded phyllitic slate / Dharamsala Sandstone strata. Under dry baseline conditions, limit equilibrium stability analysis (Hoek & Bray planar cleft-water mechanics) yields FoS = 1.30 (marginal). During monsoon steady-seepage saturation with active joint cleft-water hydrostatic pressure (zw = 1.2m), calculated FoS drops to 0.72, confirming active shear mobilization along daylighting joint set J1 (slip plane inclined length L_slip = 6.856 m). Following multi-barrier stabilization, post-remediation FoS is verified at 1.85. The site lies in Seismic Zone V (Z = 0.36, ah = 0.09g).
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.disclaimer: Subsurface geotechnical parameters (effective cohesion c' = 14.0 kPa, effective internal friction angle φ' = 28.0°, intact rock UCS = 35.0 MPa, and structural joint dip = 57.0°) are preliminary model estimates and assumptions based on empirical rock mass classifications and regional lithological analogs. These values are strictly subject to confirmatory site investigation, trial-pit logging, and rotary borehole core extraction with laboratory testing prior to detailed engineering design, statutory tendering, or construction authorization.

tier_3_statutory_directives.title: Tier 3: Statutory Remediation Directives & Civil Schedule (Imperative Standards)
tier_3_statutory_directives.description:
1. Construct a 22m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H_stem=4.50m, D_f=1.00m, Base B=2.93m, Top b=1.00m, volume = 194.54 m³ M15 with 40% plums per IS:14458 Part 2), backed by 118.80 m³ filter pack and 0 Nos. weep holes.
2. Install 25 Nos. Ø25mm High-Yield Fe500D soil nails (23 working in 1.8m H × 2.0m V grid + 2 sacrificial pullout verification test nails) drilled to 9.0m depth (180m drill, 190m bar, 18 pads, 91.12 m² wire mesh) per MoRTH Section 3100.
3. Install 5 Nos. × 15m (75.0m total) sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains (Ø75mm, Schedule 80) at 5°–10° upward rake, paired with 25.0m crest saucer catch drain (0.60m × 0.60m), 17.0m roadside drain (0.60m × 0.60m), and 22.0m stepped cascade chute per MoRTH Section 300.
4. Lay 700 GSM coir geotextile netting (0.00 m² with 10% overlap), hydroseeding, and Vetiver grass contour hedges per MoRTH Section 1802.

usgs_classification.usgs_general_definition: A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement.
usgs_classification.usgs_kinematic_definition: A downslope movement of rock or soil, or both, occurring on the surface of rupture—either curved (rotational slide) or planar (translational slide) rupture—in which much of the material often moves as a coherent or semicoherent mass with little internal deformation.
usgs_classification.material_definition: Soil containing a significant proportion of coarse fragments; 20% to 80% of the particles are greater than 2 mm in size (gravel, cobbles, and boulders).
usgs_classification.movement_definition: A slide in which the surface of rupture is curved concavely upward (spoon-shaped) and the slide movement is roughly rotational about an axis parallel to the ground surface.

velocity_class.consequences: Escape possible; property and structures destroyed; roads severely disrupted.

landslide_anatomy.crown_and_scarp: Undisplaced crown with open extensional crown cracks; distinct steep main scarp exposing rupture surface.
landslide_anatomy.displaced_mass: Depleted mass above planar/rotational surface of rupture, extending downslope into zone of accumulation.
landslide_anatomy.toe_and_foot: Displaced foot advancing beyond toe of rupture surface across roadway/property margin.

geological: Weak, weathered, or fractured rock and soil materials
Adversely oriented structural discontinuities (faults, joints, bedding planes daylighting into cut face)
morphological: Fluvial or wave erosion undermining the slope toe
Tectonic or steep gravitational escarpment oversteepening
physical_trigger: Prolonged antecedent precipitation and high-intensity storm rainfall
Transient perched groundwater table development and loss of matric suction
human_causes: Anthropogenic excavation / toe undercutting for roadway benching or foundation cuts

usgs_classification.usgs_general_definition: A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement.
usgs_classification.usgs_kinematic_definition: A downslope movement of rock or soil, or both, occurring on the surface of rupture—either curved (rotational slide) or planar (translational slide) rupture—in which much of the material often moves as a coherent or semicoherent mass with little internal deformation.
usgs_classification.material_definition: Soil containing a significant proportion of coarse fragments; 20% to 80% of the particles are greater than 2 mm in size (gravel, cobbles, and boulders).
usgs_classification.movement_definition: A slide in which the surface of rupture is curved concavely upward (spoon-shaped) and the slide movement is roughly rotational about an axis parallel to the ground surface.

velocity_class.consequences: Escape possible; property and structures destroyed; roads severely disrupted.

landslide_anatomy.crown_and_scarp: Undisplaced crown with open extensional crown cracks; distinct steep main scarp exposing rupture surface.
landslide_anatomy.displaced_mass: Depleted mass above planar/rotational surface of rupture, extending downslope into zone of accumulation.
landslide_anatomy.toe_and_foot: Displaced foot advancing beyond toe of rupture surface across roadway/property margin.

geological: Weak, weathered, or fractured rock and soil materials
Adversely oriented structural discontinuities (faults, joints, bedding planes daylighting into cut face)
morphological: Fluvial or wave erosion undermining the slope toe
Tectonic or steep gravitational escarpment oversteepening
physical_trigger: Prolonged antecedent precipitation and high-intensity storm rainfall
Transient perched groundwater table development and loss of matric suction
human_causes: Anthropogenic excavation / toe undercutting for roadway benching or foundation cuts
Surcharge loading at the slope crest (unengineered spoil disposal or building construction)

tier_1_factual_evidence.title: Tier 1: Factual Ground Truth & Telemetry (Objective Past Passive)
tier_1_factual_evidence.description: At Mandi Sector — Hill Road Corridor (Mandi Sector), a detachment scarp of vertical height 16.00 m (upper face 16.00 m inclined at 66°) was surveyed. Saturated shali dolomite & sundernagar quartzite with interbedded phyllitic slate / dharamsala sandstone debris (64.7 m³ in-situ / 80.85 m³ bulked calculated via Simpson's prismoidal rule at 1.25 bulking factor) encroached 3.10 m across the 5.50 m carriageway formation. Roadside drainage was 100% obstructed under active hydrostatic surcharge. Prior to failure, the cut slope was an unprotected excavation. Discontinuities dipping 68° adversely into the slope face were measured with aperture 15–40 mm.

tier_2_analytical_mechanics.title: Tier 2: Analytical Geotechnical Mechanics & FoS (Calibrated Engineering Inferences)
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.description: Under the Cruden & Varnes (1996) and USGS Circular 1325 classification, the failure is designated as a Rockfall / Topple Mass Movement (Cruden & Varnes, 1996) within Shali Dolomite & Sundernagar Quartzite with interbedded phyllitic slate / Dharamsala Sandstone strata. Under dry baseline conditions, limit equilibrium stability analysis (Hoek & Bray planar cleft-water mechanics) yields FoS = 1.01 (marginal). During monsoon steady-seepage saturation with active joint cleft-water hydrostatic pressure (zw = 1.2m), calculated FoS drops to 0.57, confirming active shear mobilization along daylighting joint set J1 (slip plane inclined length L_slip = 6.856 m). Following multi-barrier stabilization, post-remediation FoS is verified at 1.50. The site lies in Seismic Zone V (Z = 0.36, ah = 0.09g).
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.disclaimer: Subsurface geotechnical parameters (effective cohesion c' = 14.0 kPa, effective internal friction angle φ' = 28.0°, intact rock UCS = 35.0 MPa, and structural joint dip = 57.0°) are preliminary model estimates and assumptions based on empirical rock mass classifications and regional lithological analogs. These values are strictly subject to confirmatory site investigation, trial-pit logging, and rotary borehole core extraction with laboratory testing prior to detailed engineering design, statutory tendering, or construction authorization.

tier_3_statutory_directives.title: Tier 3: Statutory Remediation Directives & Civil Schedule (Imperative Standards)
tier_3_statutory_directives.description:
1. Construct a 21m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H_stem=0.80m, D_f=0.40m, Base B=0.60m, Top b=0.40m, volume = 8.40 m³ M15 with 40% plums per IS:14458 Part 2), backed by 0.00 m³ filter pack and 0 Nos. weep holes.
2. Install 37 Nos. Ø25mm High-Yield Fe500D soil nails (35 working in 1.8m H × 2.0m V grid + 2 sacrificial pullout verification test nails) drilled to 9.0m depth (180m drill, 190m bar, 18 pads, 91.12 m² wire mesh) per MoRTH Section 3100.
3. Install 5 Nos. × 15m (75.0m total) sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains (Ø75mm, Schedule 80) at 5°–10° upward rake, paired with 25.0m crest saucer catch drain (0.60m × 0.60m), 17.0m roadside drain (0.60m × 0.60m), and 22.0m stepped cascade chute per MoRTH Section 300.
4. Lay 700 GSM coir geotextile netting (0.00 m² with 10% overlap), hydroseeding, and Vetiver grass contour hedges per MoRTH Section 1802.

usgs_classification.usgs_general_definition: A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement.
usgs_classification.usgs_kinematic_definition: A downslope movement of rock or soil, or both, occurring on the surface of rupture—either curved (rotational slide) or planar (translational slide) rupture—in which much of the material often moves as a coherent or semicoherent mass with little internal deformation.
usgs_classification.material_definition: A hard or firm mass that was intact and in its natural place before the initiation of movement.
usgs_classification.movement_definition: Detachment of soil or rock from a steep slope or cliff along a surface with little or no shear displacement; material descends primarily through the air by falling, bouncing, or rolling.

velocity_class.consequences: Loss of life expected; some temporary evacuation possible; structures destroyed.

landslide_anatomy.crown_and_scarp: Undisplaced crown with open extensional crown cracks; distinct steep main scarp exposing rupture surface.
landslide_anatomy.displaced_mass: Depleted mass above planar/rotational surface of rupture, extending downslope into zone of accumulation.
landslide_anatomy.toe_and_foot: Displaced foot advancing beyond toe of rupture surface across roadway/property margin.

geological: Weak, weathered, or fractured rock and soil materials
Adversely oriented structural discontinuities (faults, joints, bedding planes daylighting into cut face)
morphological: Fluvial or wave erosion undermining the slope toe
Tectonic or steep gravitational escarpment oversteepening
physical_trigger: Prolonged antecedent precipitation and high-intensity storm rainfall
Transient perched groundwater table development and loss of matric suction
human_causes: Anthropogenic excavation / toe undercutting for roadway benching or foundation cuts
Surcharge loading at the slope crest (unengineered spoil disposal or building construction)

usgs_classification.usgs_general_definition: A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement.
usgs_classification.usgs_kinematic_definition: A downslope movement of rock or soil, or both, occurring on the surface of rupture—either curved (rotational slide) or planar (translational slide) rupture—in which much of the material often moves as a coherent or semicoherent mass with little internal deformation.
usgs_classification.material_definition: A hard or firm mass that was intact and in its natural place before the initiation of movement.
usgs_classification.movement_definition: Detachment of soil or rock from a steep slope or cliff along a surface with little or no shear displacement; material descends primarily through the air by falling, bouncing, or rolling.

velocity_class.consequences: Loss of life expected; some temporary evacuation possible; structures destroyed.

landslide_anatomy.crown_and_scarp: Undisplaced crown with open extensional crown cracks; distinct steep main scarp exposing rupture surface.
landslide_anatomy.displaced_mass: Depleted mass above planar/rotational surface of rupture, extending downslope into zone of accumulation.
landslide_anatomy.toe_and_foot: Displaced foot advancing beyond toe of rupture surface across roadway/property margin.

geological: Weak, weathered, or fractured rock and soil materials
Adversely oriented structural discontinuities (faults, joints, bedding planes daylighting into cut face)
morphological: Fluvial or wave erosion undermining the slope toe
Tectonic or steep gravitational escarpment oversteepening
physical_trigger: Prolonged antecedent precipitation and high-intensity storm rainfall
Transient perched groundwater table development and loss of matric suction
human_causes: Anthropogenic excavation / toe undercutting for roadway benching or foundation cuts
Surcharge loading at the slope crest (unengineered spoil disposal or building construction)

usgs_classification.standard_reference: USGS Circular 1325 (Highland & Bobrowsky, 2008) & Cruden & Varnes (1996) TRB Special Report 247

tier_1_factual_evidence.title: Tier 1: Factual Ground Truth & Telemetry (Objective Past Passive)
tier_1_factual_evidence.description: At Kinnaur Sector — Hill Road Corridor (Kinnaur Sector), a detachment scarp of vertical height 16.00 m (upper face 16.00 m inclined at 66°) was surveyed. Saturated vaikrita higher himalayan granitic gneiss, kyanite schist & pegmatite debris (64.7 m³ in-situ / 80.85 m³ bulked calculated via Simpson's prismoidal rule at 1.25 bulking factor) encroached 3.10 m across the 5.50 m carriageway formation. Roadside drainage was 100% obstructed under active hydrostatic surcharge. Prior to failure, the cut slope was an unprotected excavation. Discontinuities dipping 68° adversely into the slope face were measured with aperture 15–40 mm.
tier_1_factual_evidence.weathering_grade: Grade II to III (Slightly to Moderately Weathered with frost riving)

tier_2_analytical_mechanics.title: Tier 2: Analytical Geotechnical Mechanics & FoS (Calibrated Engineering Inferences)
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.description: Under the Cruden & Varnes (1996) and USGS Circular 1325 classification, the failure is designated as a Rockfall / Topple Mass Movement (Cruden & Varnes, 1996) within Vaikrita Higher Himalayan Granitic Gneiss, Kyanite Schist & Pegmatite strata. Under dry baseline conditions, limit equilibrium stability analysis (Hoek & Bray planar cleft-water mechanics) yields FoS = 1.01 (marginal). During monsoon steady-seepage saturation with active joint cleft-water hydrostatic pressure (zw = 1.2m), calculated FoS drops to 0.57, confirming active shear mobilization along daylighting joint set J1 (slip plane inclined length L_slip = 6.856 m). Following multi-barrier stabilization, post-remediation FoS is verified at 1.50. The site lies in Seismic Zone V (Z = 0.36, ah = 0.09g).
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.disclaimer: Subsurface geotechnical parameters (effective cohesion c' = 14.0 kPa, effective internal friction angle φ' = 28.0°, intact rock UCS = 35.0 MPa, and structural joint dip = 57.0°) are preliminary model estimates and assumptions based on empirical rock mass classifications and regional lithological analogs. These values are strictly subject to confirmatory site investigation, trial-pit logging, and rotary borehole core extraction with laboratory testing prior to detailed engineering design, statutory tendering, or construction authorization.

tier_3_statutory_directives.title: Tier 3: Statutory Remediation Directives & Civil Schedule (Imperative Standards)
tier_3_statutory_directives.description:
1. Construct a 21m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H_stem=0.80m, D_f=0.40m, Base B=0.60m, Top b=0.40m, volume = 8.40 m³ M15 with 40% plums per IS:14458 Part 2), backed by 0.00 m³ filter pack and 0 Nos. weep holes.
2. Install 37 Nos. Ø25mm High-Yield Fe500D soil nails (35 working in 1.8m H × 2.0m V grid + 2 sacrificial pullout verification test nails) drilled to 9.0m depth (180m drill, 190m bar, 18 pads, 91.12 m² wire mesh) per MoRTH Section 3100.
3. Install 5 Nos. × 15m (75.0m total) sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains (Ø75mm, Schedule 80) at 5°–10° upward rake, paired with 25.0m crest saucer catch drain (0.60m × 0.60m), 17.0m roadside drain (0.60m × 0.60m), and 22.0m stepped cascade chute per MoRTH Section 300.
4. Lay 700 GSM coir geotextile netting (0.00 m² with 10% overlap), hydroseeding, and Vetiver grass contour hedges per MoRTH Section 1802.

usgs_classification.usgs_general_definition: A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement.
usgs_classification.usgs_kinematic_definition: A downslope movement of rock or soil, or both, occurring on the surface of rupture—either curved (rotational slide) or planar (translational slide) rupture—in which much of the material often moves as a coherent or semicoherent mass with little internal deformation.
usgs_classification.material_definition: A hard or firm mass that was intact and in its natural place before the initiation of movement.
usgs_classification.movement_definition: Detachment of soil or rock from a steep slope or cliff along a surface with little or no shear displacement; material descends primarily through the air by falling, bouncing, or rolling.

velocity_class.consequences: Loss of life expected; some temporary evacuation possible; structures destroyed.

landslide_anatomy.crown_and_scarp: Undisplaced crown with open extensional crown cracks; distinct steep main scarp exposing rupture surface.
landslide_anatomy.displaced_mass: Depleted mass above planar/rotational surface of rupture, extending downslope into zone of accumulation.
landslide_anatomy.toe_and_foot: Displaced foot advancing beyond toe of rupture surface across roadway/property margin.

geological: Weak, weathered, or fractured rock and soil materials
Adversely oriented structural discontinuities (faults, joints, bedding planes daylighting into cut face)
morphological: Fluvial or wave erosion undermining the slope toe
Tectonic or steep gravitational escarpment oversteepening
physical_trigger: Prolonged antecedent precipitation and high-intensity storm rainfall
Transient perched groundwater table development and loss of matric suction
human_causes: Anthropogenic excavation / toe undercutting for roadway benching or foundation cuts
Surcharge loading at the slope crest (unengineered spoil disposal or building construction)

usgs_classification.standard_reference: USGS Circular 1325 (Highland & Bobrowsky, 2008) & Cruden & Varnes (1996) TRB Special Report 247
