usgs_classification.usgs_general_definition: A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement.
usgs_classification.usgs_kinematic_definition: A downslope movement of rock or soil, or both, occurring on the surface of rupture—either curved (rotational slide) or planar (translational slide) rupture—in which much of the material often moves as a coherent or semicoherent mass with little internal deformation.
usgs_classification.material_definition: Soil containing a significant proportion of coarse fragments; 20% to 80% of the particles are greater than 2 mm in size (gravel, cobbles, and boulders).
usgs_classification.movement_definition: A landslide mass that moves out, or down and outward, along a relatively planar surface with little rotational movement or backward tilting; frequently controlled by structural discontinuities (bedding, joints, faults).

velocity_class.consequences: Escape possible; property and structures destroyed; roads severely disrupted.

landslide_anatomy.crown_and_scarp: Undisplaced crown with open extensional crown cracks; distinct steep main scarp exposing rupture surface.
landslide_anatomy.displaced_mass: Depleted mass above planar/rotational surface of rupture, extending downslope into zone of accumulation.
landslide_anatomy.toe_and_foot: Displaced foot advancing beyond toe of rupture surface across roadway/property margin.

geological: Weak, weathered, or fractured rock and soil materials
Adversely oriented structural discontinuities (faults, joints, bedding planes daylighting into cut face)
morphological: Fluvial or wave erosion undermining the slope toe
Tectonic or steep gravitational escarpment oversteepening
physical_trigger: Prolonged antecedent precipitation and high-intensity storm rainfall
Transient perched groundwater table development and loss of matric suction
human_causes: Anthropogenic excavation / toe undercutting for roadway benching or foundation cuts
Surcharge loading at the slope crest (unengineered spoil disposal or building construction)

usgs_classification.usgs_general_definition: A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement.
usgs_classification.usgs_kinematic_definition: A downslope movement of rock or soil, or both, occurring on the surface of rupture—either curved (rotational slide) or planar (translational slide) rupture—in which much of the material often moves as a coherent or semicoherent mass with little internal deformation.
usgs_classification.material_definition: Soil containing a significant proportion of coarse fragments; 20% to 80% of the particles are greater than 2 mm in size (gravel, cobbles, and boulders).
usgs_classification.movement_definition: A landslide mass that moves out, or down and outward, along a relatively planar surface with little rotational movement or backward tilting; frequently controlled by structural discontinuities (bedding, joints, faults).

velocity_class.consequences: Escape possible; property and structures destroyed; roads severely disrupted.

landslide_anatomy.crown_and_scarp: Undisplaced crown with open extensional crown cracks; distinct steep main scarp exposing rupture surface.
landslide_anatomy.displaced_mass: Depleted mass above planar/rotational surface of rupture, extending downslope into zone of accumulation.
landslide_anatomy.toe_and_foot: Displaced foot advancing beyond toe of rupture surface across roadway/property margin.

geological: Weak, weathered, or fractured rock and soil materials
Adversely oriented structural discontinuities (faults, joints, bedding planes daylighting into cut face)
morphological: Fluvial or wave erosion undermining the slope toe
Tectonic or steep gravitational escarpment oversteepening
physical_trigger: Prolonged antecedent precipitation and high-intensity storm rainfall
Transient perched groundwater table development and loss of matric suction
human_causes: Anthropogenic excavation / toe undercutting for roadway benching or foundation cuts
Surcharge loading at the slope crest (unengineered spoil disposal or building construction)

usgs_classification.standard_reference: USGS Circular 1325 (Highland & Bobrowsky, 2008) & Cruden & Varnes (1996) TRB Special Report 247

HL-CR-17525F02.mitigation_measures:
1. Primary Toe Retention & Structural Retention (IS:14458 Part 2 / MoRTH Section 1500):
   Emergency clearance of 181.2 m³ bulked debris (145.0 m³ in-situ @ 1.25 bulking) followed by construction of a 17.0m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H_stem = 2.70m, D_f = 1.00m embedment, base width B = 1.35m, concrete volume = 67.70 m³ M15 with 40% plums), backed by 16.07 m³ crushed gravel filter pack wrapped in 67.25 m² non-woven geotextile and 26 Nos. PVC weep holes.
2. Internal Ground Reinforcement & Slope Nailing (MoRTH Section 3100 / CEDD Geoguide 7):
   Installation of 20 Nos. Ø25mm High-Yield Fe500D TMT soil nails (18 working nails + 2 sacrificial test nails) drilled to 9.0m depth (180.0m total drilling), pressure grouted with non-shrink cementitious grout, anchored with RC bearing pads and high-tensile diamond steel wire mesh facing (91.12 m²).
3. Hydrogeological Pore-Pressure Relief & Surface Drainage (MoRTH Section 300, Clause 309 / IRC:SP:48):
   Installation of 5 Nos. × 15m (75.0m total) sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains (Ø75mm, Schedule 80) drilled at 5°–10° upward rake into the hillside, accompanied by crest catch drain, roadside drain, and cascade chute.
4. Soil Bioengineering & Surficial Erosion Control (MoRTH Section 1802 / IS:14458):
   Dressing cut face (91.12 m²), laying 700 GSM coir geotextile netting (100.23 m² with 10% overlap), hydraulic hydroseeding, and planting Vetiver grass contour hedges.
HL-CR-17525F02.other_observations: Sub-surface groundwater seepage daylighting along the colluvial mantle and bedrock interface, confirming elevated perched phreatic levels during rainfall. Active extensional tension fissures (apertures 15-40 mm) trace uphill of the detachment crown. Relict discontinuity set J1 (57° dip daylighting adversely into the slope face) exhibits planar persistent slickensides with iron-oxide staining, confirming kinematic daylighting and high susceptibility to progressive retrogressive failure during prolonged monsoon precipitation.

HL-CR-17525F02.synthesis_remarks:
1. GEOTECHNICAL & KINEMATIC CLASSIFICATION (USGS Circular 1325 / Cruden & Varnes 1996):

2. CONSEQUENCE RATING & LIMIT STATE STABILITY (CEDD Geoguide 1 / Eurocode 7):
Under Hong Kong CEDD Geoguide 1 consequence classification, this corridor represents Category 2 (High / Sub-Divisional Transport Consequence). Prior to failure, the slope had a dry baseline FoS of 1.01, which dropped to FoS = 0.60 under monsoon cleft-water hydrostatic saturation, causing active shear mobilization. - Pore-Pressure Relief Drainage: 5 Nos. × 15m (75.0m total) Ø75mm Schedule 80 slotted PVC relief drains at 5°–10° upward rake paired with crest catch drain and cascade chute.
- Bioengineering: 700 GSM coir geotextile netting (100.23 m² with 10% overlap), hydroseeding, and Vetiver grass contour hedges (MoRTH 1802).

tier_1_factual_evidence.title: Tier 1: Factual Ground Truth & Telemetry (Objective Past Passive)
tier_1_factual_evidence.description: At Mandi Sector — Hill Road Corridor (Mandi Sector), a detachment scarp of vertical height 7.60 m (upper face 4.90 m inclined at 66°) was surveyed. Saturated shali dolomite & sundernagar quartzite with interbedded phyllitic slate / dharamsala sandstone debris (145.0 m³ in-situ / 181.25 m³ bulked calculated via Simpson's prismoidal rule at 1.25 bulking factor) encroached 2.95 m across the 5.25 m carriageway formation. Roadside drainage was 100% obstructed under active hydrostatic surcharge. Prior to failure, the cut slope was an unprotected excavation. Discontinuities dipping 57° adversely into the slope face were measured with aperture 15–40 mm.

tier_2_analytical_mechanics.title: Tier 2: Analytical Geotechnical Mechanics & FoS (Calibrated Engineering Inferences)
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.description: Under the Cruden & Varnes (1996) and USGS Circular 1325 classification, the failure is designated as a Slide Mass Movement (Cruden & Varnes, 1996) within Shali Dolomite & Sundernagar Quartzite with interbedded phyllitic slate / Dharamsala Sandstone strata. Under dry baseline conditions, limit equilibrium stability analysis (Hoek & Bray planar cleft-water mechanics) yields FoS = 1.01 (marginal). During monsoon steady-seepage saturation with active joint cleft-water hydrostatic pressure (zw = 1.2m), calculated FoS drops to 0.60, confirming active shear mobilization along daylighting joint set J1 (slip plane inclined length L_slip = 6.856 m). Following multi-barrier stabilization, post-remediation FoS is verified at 1.54. The site lies in Seismic Zone V (Z = 0.36, ah = 0.09g).
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.disclaimer: Subsurface geotechnical parameters (effective cohesion c' = 14.0 kPa, effective internal friction angle φ' = 28.0°, intact rock UCS = 35.0 MPa, and structural joint dip = 57.0°) are preliminary model estimates and assumptions based on empirical rock mass classifications and regional lithological analogs. These values are strictly subject to confirmatory site investigation, trial-pit logging, and rotary borehole core extraction with laboratory testing prior to detailed engineering design, statutory tendering, or construction authorization.

tier_3_statutory_directives.title: Tier 3: Statutory Remediation Directives & Civil Schedule (Imperative Standards)
tier_3_statutory_directives.description:
1. Construct a 17m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H_stem=2.70m, D_f=1.00m, Base B=1.35m, Top b=0.60m, volume = 67.70 m³ M15 with 40% plums per IS:14458 Part 2), backed by 16.07 m³ filter pack and 26 Nos. weep holes.
2. Install 20 Nos. Ø25mm High-Yield Fe500D soil nails (18 working in 1.8m H × 2.0m V grid + 2 sacrificial pullout verification test nails) drilled to 9.0m depth (180m drill, 190m bar, 18 pads, 91.12 m² wire mesh) per MoRTH Section 3100.
3. Install 5 Nos. × 15m (75.0m total) sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains (Ø75mm, Schedule 80) at 5°–10° upward rake, paired with 25.0m crest saucer catch drain (0.60m × 0.60m), 17.0m roadside drain (0.60m × 0.60m), and 22.0m stepped cascade chute per MoRTH Section 300.
4. Lay 700 GSM coir geotextile netting (100.23 m² with 10% overlap), hydroseeding, and Vetiver grass contour hedges per MoRTH Section 1802.

boq_items.description: Installation of sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains (Ø75mm, Schedule 80) at 5°–10° upward rake into hillside with cleanout cap. (5 Nos. × 15m)

boq_items.short_description: Coir geotextile netting (700 GSM), hydroseeding & Vetiver grass contour hedges

usgs_classification.usgs_general_definition: A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement.
usgs_classification.usgs_kinematic_definition: A downslope movement of rock or soil, or both, occurring on the surface of rupture—either curved (rotational slide) or planar (translational slide) rupture—in which much of the material often moves as a coherent or semicoherent mass with little internal deformation.
usgs_classification.material_definition: Soil containing a significant proportion of coarse fragments; 20% to 80% of the particles are greater than 2 mm in size (gravel, cobbles, and boulders).
usgs_classification.movement_definition: A landslide mass that moves out, or down and outward, along a relatively planar surface with little rotational movement or backward tilting; frequently controlled by structural discontinuities (bedding, joints, faults).

velocity_class.consequences: Escape possible; property and structures destroyed; roads severely disrupted.

landslide_anatomy.crown_and_scarp: Undisplaced crown with open extensional crown cracks; distinct steep main scarp exposing rupture surface.
landslide_anatomy.displaced_mass: Depleted mass above planar/rotational surface of rupture, extending downslope into zone of accumulation.
landslide_anatomy.toe_and_foot: Displaced foot advancing beyond toe of rupture surface across roadway/property margin.

geological: Weak, weathered, or fractured rock and soil materials
Adversely oriented structural discontinuities (faults, joints, bedding planes daylighting into cut face)
morphological: Fluvial or wave erosion undermining the slope toe
Tectonic or steep gravitational escarpment oversteepening
physical_trigger: Prolonged antecedent precipitation and high-intensity storm rainfall
Transient perched groundwater table development and loss of matric suction
human_causes: Anthropogenic excavation / toe undercutting for roadway benching or foundation cuts
Surcharge loading at the slope crest (unengineered spoil disposal or building construction)

usgs_classification.standard_reference: USGS Circular 1325 (Highland & Bobrowsky, 2008) & Cruden & Varnes (1996) TRB Special Report 247

bhukosh_geology.citation: Rahul V. et al., 2016. Macro-scale (1:50,000) landslide susceptibility Mapping in parts of toposheets no. 53A/13, 14, Kullu and Mandi districts, Himachal Pradesh. Unpub. GSI report of FS 2015-2016

IITM-STAR-17525F02.mitigation_measures:
1. Primary Toe Retention & Structural Retention (IS:14458 Part 2 / MoRTH Section 1500):
   Emergency clearance of 181.2 m³ bulked debris (145.0 m³ in-situ @ 1.25 bulking) followed by construction of a 17.0m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H_stem = 2.70m, D_f = 1.00m embedment, base width B = 1.35m, concrete volume = 67.70 m³ M15 with 40% plums), backed by 16.07 m³ crushed gravel filter pack wrapped in 67.25 m² non-woven geotextile and 26 Nos. PVC weep holes.
2. Internal Ground Reinforcement & Slope Nailing (MoRTH Section 3100 / CEDD Geoguide 7):
   Installation of 20 Nos. Ø25mm High-Yield Fe500D TMT soil nails (18 working nails + 2 sacrificial test nails) drilled to 9.0m depth (180.0m total drilling), pressure grouted with non-shrink cementitious grout, anchored with RC bearing pads and high-tensile diamond steel wire mesh facing (91.12 m²).
3. Hydrogeological Pore-Pressure Relief & Surface Drainage (MoRTH Section 300, Clause 309 / IRC:SP:48):
   Installation of 5 Nos. × 15m (75.0m total) sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains (Ø75mm, Schedule 80) drilled at 5°–10° upward rake into the hillside, accompanied by crest catch drain, roadside drain, and cascade chute.
4. Soil Bioengineering & Surficial Erosion Control (MoRTH Section 1802 / IS:14458):
   Dressing cut face (91.12 m²), laying 700 GSM coir geotextile netting (100.23 m² with 10% overlap), hydraulic hydroseeding, and planting Vetiver grass contour hedges.
IITM-STAR-17525F02.other_observations: Sub-surface groundwater seepage daylighting along the colluvial mantle and bedrock interface, confirming elevated perched phreatic levels during rainfall. Active extensional tension fissures (apertures 15-40 mm) trace uphill of the detachment crown. Relict discontinuity set J1 (57° dip daylighting adversely into the slope face) exhibits planar persistent slickensides with iron-oxide staining, confirming kinematic daylighting and high susceptibility to progressive retrogressive failure during prolonged monsoon precipitation.

IITM-STAR-17525F02.synthesis_remarks:
1. GEOTECHNICAL & KINEMATIC CLASSIFICATION (USGS Circular 1325 / Cruden & Varnes 1996):
Forensic geotechnical evaluation of the Mandi Sector — Hill Road Corridor (31.70800° N, 76.93200° E) confirms an active slope failure formally designated under Cruden & Varnes (1996) taxonomy as Slide Mass Movement (Cruden & Varnes, 1996). The failure detachment occurred in Shali Dolomite & Sundernagar Quartzite with interbedded phyllitic slate / Dharamsala Sandstone bedrock, releasing 145.0 m³ in-situ (181.25 m³ bulked @ 1.25 swell) of colluvial overburden across the corridor.

2. CONSEQUENCE RATING & LIMIT STATE STABILITY (CEDD Geoguide 1 / Eurocode 7):
Under Hong Kong CEDD Geoguide 1 consequence classification, this corridor represents Category 2 (High / Sub-Divisional Transport Consequence). Prior to failure, the slope had a dry baseline FoS of 1.01, which dropped to FoS = 0.60 under monsoon cleft-water hydrostatic saturation, causing active shear mobilization. Post-stabilization analysis yields a verified FoS = 1.54, satisfying statutory design thresholds.

3. MULTI-BARRIER MITIGATION STRATEGY (IS:14458 / MoRTH Section 3100 / CEDD Geoguide 7):
- Primary Toe Retention: Construction of a 17.0m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H_stem = 2.70m, D_f = 1.00m, base width B = 1.35m, concrete volume = 67.70 m³ M15 with 40% plums per IS:14458 Part 2) with 16.07 m³ granular filter pack and 26 Nos. weep holes.
- Internal Ground Reinforcement: Prescribed Soil Nailing Array (20 Nos. @ 18 working + 2 test, 180.0m drill, 91.12 m² mesh facing, MoRTH 3100).
- Pore-Pressure Relief Drainage: 5 Nos. × 15m (75.0m total) Ø75mm Schedule 80 slotted PVC relief drains at 5°–10° upward rake paired with crest catch drain and cascade chute.
- Bioengineering: 700 GSM coir geotextile netting (100.23 m² with 10% overlap), hydroseeding, and Vetiver grass contour hedges (MoRTH 1802).

4. STATUTORY ESTIMATE & REQUISITION HEADS:
Total Direct Civil Remediation Outlay is dynamically estimated at ₹ 960,304.90 (Subtotal A). With statutory contingency, quality control, and 18% GST, the Total Civil Remediation Outlay is ₹ 1,184,151.97. Direct physical asset damage (SDRF) is strictly segregated from contractor procurement.

5. ENGINEERING DISCLAIMER & GEOTECHNICAL LIMITATION:
Subsurface geotechnical parameters (effective cohesion c' = 14.0 kPa, effective internal friction angle φ' = 28.0°, intact rock UCS = 35.0 MPa, and structural joint dip = 57.0°) are preliminary model estimates and assumptions based on empirical rock mass classifications and regional lithological analogs. These values are strictly subject to confirmatory site investigation, trial-pit logging, and rotary borehole core extraction with laboratory testing prior to detailed engineering design, statutory tendering, or construction authorization.

plain_language_explanation.summary_title: Slope Incident Assessment — Mandi Sector — Hill Road Corridor
plain_language_explanation.what_happened: A steep section of the hillside failed, depositing approximately 181 m³ of colluvial debris and boulders across the corridor.
plain_language_explanation.why_it_happened: Heavy precipitation saturated structural discontinuities dipping 57° into the formation, inducing hydrostatic cleft-water pressure and shear displacement.
plain_language_explanation.property_and_access_impact: Passage is obstructed (2.95 m (Single-Lane Restricted / Shoulder Lost: 2.30m Operable)). Single-lane transit is restricted under safety spotters.
plain_language_explanation.road_and_travel_impact: Passage is obstructed (2.95 m (Single-Lane Restricted / Shoulder Lost: 2.30m Operable)). Single-lane transit is restricted under safety spotters.
plain_language_explanation.ongoing_hazards: The hillside directly above remains vulnerable to secondary detachment under continuous precipitation.
plain_language_explanation.what_needs_to_be_done: Deploy machinery to clear 181 m³ of debris, construct a 17m retaining wall, install soil nails, and drill subsurface drainage.
plain_language_explanation.citizen_safety_advice: Do NOT attempt to transit under active scarp faces during rainfall. Follow flagger directions and maintain safe exclusion distance.

tier_1_factual_evidence.title: Tier 1: Factual Ground Truth & Telemetry (Objective Past Passive)
tier_1_factual_evidence.description: At Mandi Sector — Hill Road Corridor (Mandi Sector), a detachment scarp of vertical height 7.60 m (upper face 4.90 m inclined at 66°) was surveyed. Saturated shali dolomite & sundernagar quartzite with interbedded phyllitic slate / dharamsala sandstone debris (145.0 m³ in-situ / 181.25 m³ bulked calculated via Simpson's prismoidal rule at 1.25 bulking factor) encroached 2.95 m across the 5.25 m carriageway formation. Roadside drainage was 100% obstructed under active hydrostatic surcharge. Prior to failure, the cut slope was an unprotected excavation. Discontinuities dipping 57° adversely into the slope face were measured with aperture 15–40 mm.

tier_2_analytical_mechanics.title: Tier 2: Analytical Geotechnical Mechanics & FoS (Calibrated Engineering Inferences)
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.description: Under the Cruden & Varnes (1996) and USGS Circular 1325 classification, the failure is designated as a Slide Mass Movement (Cruden & Varnes, 1996) within Shali Dolomite & Sundernagar Quartzite with interbedded phyllitic slate / Dharamsala Sandstone strata. Under dry baseline conditions, limit equilibrium stability analysis (Hoek & Bray planar cleft-water mechanics) yields FoS = 1.01 (marginal). During monsoon steady-seepage saturation with active joint cleft-water hydrostatic pressure (zw = 1.2m), calculated FoS drops to 0.60, confirming active shear mobilization along daylighting joint set J1 (slip plane inclined length L_slip = 6.856 m). Following multi-barrier stabilization, post-remediation FoS is verified at 1.54. The site lies in Seismic Zone V (Z = 0.36, ah = 0.09g).
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.disclaimer: Subsurface geotechnical parameters (effective cohesion c' = 14.0 kPa, effective internal friction angle φ' = 28.0°, intact rock UCS = 35.0 MPa, and structural joint dip = 57.0°) are preliminary model estimates and assumptions based on empirical rock mass classifications and regional lithological analogs. These values are strictly subject to confirmatory site investigation, trial-pit logging, and rotary borehole core extraction with laboratory testing prior to detailed engineering design, statutory tendering, or construction authorization.

tier_3_statutory_directives.title: Tier 3: Statutory Remediation Directives & Civil Schedule (Imperative Standards)
tier_3_statutory_directives.description:
1. Construct a 17m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H_stem=2.70m, D_f=1.00m, Base B=1.35m, Top b=0.60m, volume = 67.70 m³ M15 with 40% plums per IS:14458 Part 2), backed by 16.07 m³ filter pack and 26 Nos. weep holes.
2. Install 20 Nos. Ø25mm High-Yield Fe500D soil nails (18 working in 1.8m H × 2.0m V grid + 2 sacrificial pullout verification test nails) drilled to 9.0m depth (180m drill, 190m bar, 18 pads, 91.12 m² wire mesh) per MoRTH Section 3100.
3. Install 5 Nos. × 15m (75.0m total) sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains (Ø75mm, Schedule 80) at 5°–10° upward rake, paired with 25.0m crest saucer catch drain (0.60m × 0.60m), 17.0m roadside drain (0.60m × 0.60m), and 22.0m stepped cascade chute per MoRTH Section 300.
4. Lay 700 GSM coir geotextile netting (100.23 m² with 10% overlap), hydroseeding, and Vetiver grass contour hedges per MoRTH Section 1802.

usgs_classification.usgs_general_definition: A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement.
usgs_classification.usgs_kinematic_definition: A downslope movement of rock or soil, or both, occurring on the surface of rupture—either curved (rotational slide) or planar (translational slide) rupture—in which much of the material often moves as a coherent or semicoherent mass with little internal deformation.
usgs_classification.material_definition: Soil containing a significant proportion of coarse fragments; 20% to 80% of the particles are greater than 2 mm in size (gravel, cobbles, and boulders).
usgs_classification.movement_definition: A landslide mass that moves out, or down and outward, along a relatively planar surface with little rotational movement or backward tilting; frequently controlled by structural discontinuities (bedding, joints, faults).

velocity_class.consequences: Escape possible; property and structures destroyed; roads severely disrupted.

landslide_anatomy.crown_and_scarp: Undisplaced crown with open extensional crown cracks; distinct steep main scarp exposing rupture surface.
landslide_anatomy.displaced_mass: Depleted mass above planar/rotational surface of rupture, extending downslope into zone of accumulation.
landslide_anatomy.toe_and_foot: Displaced foot advancing beyond toe of rupture surface across roadway/property margin.

geological: Weak, weathered, or fractured rock and soil materials
Adversely oriented structural discontinuities (faults, joints, bedding planes daylighting into cut face)
morphological: Fluvial or wave erosion undermining the slope toe
Tectonic or steep gravitational escarpment oversteepening
physical_trigger: Prolonged antecedent precipitation and high-intensity storm rainfall
Transient perched groundwater table development and loss of matric suction
human_causes: Anthropogenic excavation / toe undercutting for roadway benching or foundation cuts
Surcharge loading at the slope crest (unengineered spoil disposal or building construction)

usgs_classification.standard_reference: USGS Circular 1325 (Highland & Bobrowsky, 2008) & Cruden & Varnes (1996) TRB Special Report 247

usgs_classification.usgs_general_definition: A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement.
usgs_classification.usgs_kinematic_definition: A downslope movement of rock or soil, or both, occurring on the surface of rupture—either curved (rotational slide) or planar (translational slide) rupture—in which much of the material often moves as a coherent or semicoherent mass with little internal deformation.
usgs_classification.material_definition: Soil containing a significant proportion of coarse fragments; 20% to 80% of the particles are greater than 2 mm in size (gravel, cobbles, and boulders).
usgs_classification.movement_definition: A landslide mass that moves out, or down and outward, along a relatively planar surface with little rotational movement or backward tilting; frequently controlled by structural discontinuities (bedding, joints, faults).

velocity_class.consequences: Escape possible; property and structures destroyed; roads severely disrupted.

landslide_anatomy.crown_and_scarp: Undisplaced crown with open extensional crown cracks; distinct steep main scarp exposing rupture surface.
landslide_anatomy.displaced_mass: Depleted mass above planar/rotational surface of rupture, extending downslope into zone of accumulation.
landslide_anatomy.toe_and_foot: Displaced foot advancing beyond toe of rupture surface across roadway/property margin.

geological: Weak, weathered, or fractured rock and soil materials
Adversely oriented structural discontinuities (faults, joints, bedding planes daylighting into cut face)
morphological: Fluvial or wave erosion undermining the slope toe
Tectonic or steep gravitational escarpment oversteepening
physical_trigger: Prolonged antecedent precipitation and high-intensity storm rainfall
Transient perched groundwater table development and loss of matric suction
human_causes: Anthropogenic excavation / toe undercutting for roadway benching or foundation cuts
Surcharge loading at the slope crest (unengineered spoil disposal or building construction)

plain_language_explanation.summary_title: Slope Incident Assessment — Mandi Sector — Hill Road Corridor
plain_language_explanation.what_happened: A steep section of the hillside failed, depositing approximately 181 m³ of colluvial debris and boulders across the corridor.
plain_language_explanation.why_it_happened: Heavy precipitation saturated structural discontinuities dipping 57° into the formation, inducing hydrostatic cleft-water pressure and shear displacement.
plain_language_explanation.property_and_access_impact: Passage is obstructed (2.95 m (Single-Lane Restricted / Shoulder Lost: 2.30m Operable)). Single-lane transit is restricted under safety spotters.
plain_language_explanation.road_and_travel_impact: Passage is obstructed (2.95 m (Single-Lane Restricted / Shoulder Lost: 2.30m Operable)). Single-lane transit is restricted under safety spotters.
plain_language_explanation.ongoing_hazards: The hillside directly above remains vulnerable to secondary detachment under continuous precipitation.
plain_language_explanation.what_needs_to_be_done: Deploy machinery to clear 181 m³ of debris, construct a 17m retaining wall, install soil nails, and drill subsurface drainage.
plain_language_explanation.citizen_safety_advice: Do NOT attempt to transit under active scarp faces during rainfall. Follow flagger directions and maintain safe exclusion distance.
plain_language_explanation.summary: This incident report was submitted without an attached field photograph. Geotechnical stabilization measures and civil quantities cannot be calculated without photographic terrain evidence.

tier_1_factual_evidence.title: Tier 1: Factual Ground Truth & Telemetry (Objective Past Passive)
tier_1_factual_evidence.description: At Mandi Sector — Hill Road Corridor (Mandi Sector), a detachment scarp of vertical height 7.60 m (upper face 4.90 m inclined at 66°) was surveyed. Saturated shali dolomite & sundernagar quartzite with interbedded phyllitic slate / dharamsala sandstone debris (145.0 m³ in-situ / 181.25 m³ bulked calculated via Simpson's prismoidal rule at 1.25 bulking factor) encroached 2.95 m across the 5.25 m carriageway formation. Roadside drainage was 100% obstructed under active hydrostatic surcharge. Prior to failure, the cut slope was an unprotected excavation. Discontinuities dipping 57° adversely into the slope face were measured with aperture 15–40 mm.

tier_2_analytical_mechanics.title: Tier 2: Analytical Geotechnical Mechanics & FoS (Calibrated Engineering Inferences)
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.description: Under the Cruden & Varnes (1996) and USGS Circular 1325 classification, the failure is designated as a Slide Mass Movement (Cruden & Varnes, 1996) within Shali Dolomite & Sundernagar Quartzite with interbedded phyllitic slate / Dharamsala Sandstone strata. Under dry baseline conditions, limit equilibrium stability analysis (Hoek & Bray planar cleft-water mechanics) yields FoS = 1.01 (marginal). During monsoon steady-seepage saturation with active joint cleft-water hydrostatic pressure (zw = 1.2m), calculated FoS drops to 0.60, confirming active shear mobilization along daylighting joint set J1 (slip plane inclined length L_slip = 6.856 m). Following multi-barrier stabilization, post-remediation FoS is verified at 1.54. The site lies in Seismic Zone V (Z = 0.36, ah = 0.09g).
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.disclaimer: Subsurface geotechnical parameters (effective cohesion c' = 14.0 kPa, effective internal friction angle φ' = 28.0°, intact rock UCS = 35.0 MPa, and structural joint dip = 57.0°) are preliminary model estimates and assumptions based on empirical rock mass classifications and regional lithological analogs. These values are strictly subject to confirmatory site investigation, trial-pit logging, and rotary borehole core extraction with laboratory testing prior to detailed engineering design, statutory tendering, or construction authorization.

tier_3_statutory_directives.title: Tier 3: Statutory Remediation Directives & Civil Schedule (Imperative Standards)
tier_3_statutory_directives.description:
1. Construct a 17m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H_stem=2.70m, D_f=1.00m, Base B=1.35m, Top b=0.60m, volume = 67.70 m³ M15 with 40% plums per IS:14458 Part 2), backed by 16.07 m³ filter pack and 26 Nos. weep holes.
2. Install 20 Nos. Ø25mm High-Yield Fe500D soil nails (18 working in 1.8m H × 2.0m V grid + 2 sacrificial pullout verification test nails) drilled to 9.0m depth (180m drill, 190m bar, 18 pads, 91.12 m² wire mesh) per MoRTH Section 3100.
3. Install 5 Nos. × 15m (75.0m total) sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains (Ø75mm, Schedule 80) at 5°–10° upward rake, paired with 25.0m crest saucer catch drain (0.60m × 0.60m), 17.0m roadside drain (0.60m × 0.60m), and 22.0m stepped cascade chute per MoRTH Section 300.
4. Lay 700 GSM coir geotextile netting (100.23 m² with 10% overlap), hydroseeding, and Vetiver grass contour hedges per MoRTH Section 1802.

IITM-CR-61DC3C62.mitigation_measures:
1. Primary Toe Retention & Structural Retention (IS:14458 Part 2 / MoRTH Section 1500):
   Emergency clearance of 70.7 m³ bulked debris (56.5 m³ in-situ @ 1.25 bulking) followed by construction of a 15m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H_stem = 3.02m, D_f = 1.12m embedment, base width B = 1.44m, concrete volume = 70.40 m³ M15 with 40% plums), backed by 15.85 m³ crushed gravel filter pack wrapped in 64.93 m² non-woven geotextile and 24 Nos. PVC weep holes.
2. Internal Ground Reinforcement & Slope Nailing (MoRTH Section 3100 / CEDD Geoguide 7):
   Installation of 26 Nos. Ø25mm High-Yield Fe500D TMT soil nails (24 working nails + 2 sacrificial test nails) drilled to 9.0m depth (180.0m total drilling), pressure grouted with non-shrink cementitious grout, anchored with RC bearing pads and high-tensile diamond steel wire mesh facing (91.12 m²).
3. Hydrogeological Pore-Pressure Relief & Surface Drainage (MoRTH Section 300, Clause 309 / IRC:SP:48):
   Installation of 5 Nos. × 15m (75.0m total) sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains (Ø75mm, Schedule 80) drilled at 5°–10° upward rake into the hillside, accompanied by crest catch drain, roadside drain, and cascade chute.
4. Soil Bioengineering & Surficial Erosion Control (MoRTH Section 1802 / IS:14458):
   Dressing cut face (91.12 m²), laying 700 GSM coir geotextile netting (110.39 m² with 10% overlap), hydraulic hydroseeding, and planting Vetiver grass contour hedges.
IITM-CR-61DC3C62.other_observations: Sub-surface groundwater seepage daylighting along the colluvial mantle and bedrock interface, confirming elevated perched phreatic levels during rainfall. Active extensional tension fissures (apertures 15-40 mm) trace uphill of the detachment crown. Relict discontinuity set J1 (45° dip daylighting adversely into the slope face) exhibits planar persistent slickensides with iron-oxide staining, confirming kinematic daylighting and high susceptibility to progressive retrogressive failure during prolonged monsoon precipitation.

plain_language_explanation.summary_title: Hill Cut-Slope Slide Blocking Roadway
plain_language_explanation.what_happened: A section of the steep hillside has collapsed, depositing soil and rock debris onto the road surface.
plain_language_explanation.why_it_happened: The failure is likely due to the weathering of sandstone and potential saturation of the slope, causing the material to lose stability.
plain_language_explanation.property_and_access_impact: The slide has partially blocked the road, restricting traffic to a single lane and creating a hazard for commuters.
plain_language_explanation.road_and_travel_impact: The slide has partially blocked the road, restricting traffic to a single lane and creating a hazard for commuters.
plain_language_explanation.ongoing_hazards: Risk of secondary rockfall or further sliding remains high until the slope is cleared and stabilized.
plain_language_explanation.what_needs_to_be_done: Clear the debris, perform slope scaling to remove loose rocks, and construct a retaining wall to prevent further encroachment.
plain_language_explanation.citizen_safety_advice: Avoid stopping near the slide area and follow all traffic instructions provided by local authorities.

tier_1_factual_evidence.title: Tier 1: Factual Ground Truth & Telemetry (Objective Past Passive)
tier_1_factual_evidence.description: At Mandi Sector — Hill Road Corridor (Mandi Sector), a detachment scarp of vertical height 7.60 m (upper face 4.90 m inclined at 66°) was surveyed. Saturated shali dolomite & sundernagar quartzite with interbedded phyllitic slate / dharamsala sandstone debris (145.0 m³ in-situ / 181.25 m³ bulked calculated via Simpson's prismoidal rule at 1.25 bulking factor) encroached 2.95 m across the 5.25 m carriageway formation. Roadside drainage was 100% obstructed under active hydrostatic surcharge. Prior to failure, the cut slope was an unprotected excavation. Discontinuities dipping 57° adversely into the slope face were measured with aperture 15–40 mm.

tier_2_analytical_mechanics.title: Tier 2: Analytical Geotechnical Mechanics & FoS (Calibrated Engineering Inferences)
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.description: Under the Cruden & Varnes (1996) and USGS Circular 1325 classification, the failure is designated as a Slide Mass Movement (Cruden & Varnes, 1996) within Shali Dolomite & Sundernagar Quartzite with interbedded phyllitic slate / Dharamsala Sandstone strata. Under dry baseline conditions, limit equilibrium stability analysis (Hoek & Bray planar cleft-water mechanics) yields FoS = 1.01 (marginal). During monsoon steady-seepage saturation with active joint cleft-water hydrostatic pressure (zw = 1.2m), calculated FoS drops to 0.60, confirming active shear mobilization along daylighting joint set J1 (slip plane inclined length L_slip = 6.856 m). Following multi-barrier stabilization, post-remediation FoS is verified at 1.54. The site lies in Seismic Zone V (Z = 0.36, ah = 0.09g).
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.disclaimer: Subsurface geotechnical parameters (effective cohesion c' = 14.0 kPa, effective internal friction angle φ' = 28.0°, intact rock UCS = 35.0 MPa, and structural joint dip = 57.0°) are preliminary model estimates and assumptions based on empirical rock mass classifications and regional lithological analogs. These values are strictly subject to confirmatory site investigation, trial-pit logging, and rotary borehole core extraction with laboratory testing prior to detailed engineering design, statutory tendering, or construction authorization.

tier_3_statutory_directives.title: Tier 3: Statutory Remediation Directives & Civil Schedule (Imperative Standards)
tier_3_statutory_directives.description:
1. Construct a 17m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H_stem=2.70m, D_f=1.00m, Base B=1.35m, Top b=0.60m, volume = 67.70 m³ M15 with 40% plums per IS:14458 Part 2), backed by 16.07 m³ filter pack and 26 Nos. weep holes.
2. Install 20 Nos. Ø25mm High-Yield Fe500D soil nails (18 working in 1.8m H × 2.0m V grid + 2 sacrificial pullout verification test nails) drilled to 9.0m depth (180m drill, 190m bar, 18 pads, 91.12 m² wire mesh) per MoRTH Section 3100.
3. Install 5 Nos. × 15m (75.0m total) sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains (Ø75mm, Schedule 80) at 5°–10° upward rake, paired with 25.0m crest saucer catch drain (0.60m × 0.60m), 17.0m roadside drain (0.60m × 0.60m), and 22.0m stepped cascade chute per MoRTH Section 300.
4. Lay 700 GSM coir geotextile netting (100.23 m² with 10% overlap), hydroseeding, and Vetiver grass contour hedges per MoRTH Section 1802.

usgs_classification.usgs_general_definition: A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement.
usgs_classification.usgs_kinematic_definition: A downslope movement of rock or soil, or both, occurring on the surface of rupture—either curved (rotational slide) or planar (translational slide) rupture—in which much of the material often moves as a coherent or semicoherent mass with little internal deformation.
usgs_classification.material_definition: Soil containing a significant proportion of coarse fragments; 20% to 80% of the particles are greater than 2 mm in size (gravel, cobbles, and boulders).
usgs_classification.movement_definition: A landslide mass that moves out, or down and outward, along a relatively planar surface with little rotational movement or backward tilting; frequently controlled by structural discontinuities (bedding, joints, faults).

velocity_class.consequences: Escape possible; property and structures destroyed; roads severely disrupted.

landslide_anatomy.crown_and_scarp: Undisplaced crown with open extensional crown cracks; distinct steep main scarp exposing rupture surface.
landslide_anatomy.displaced_mass: Depleted mass above planar/rotational surface of rupture, extending downslope into zone of accumulation.
landslide_anatomy.toe_and_foot: Displaced foot advancing beyond toe of rupture surface across roadway/property margin.

geological: Weak, weathered, or fractured rock and soil materials
Adversely oriented structural discontinuities (faults, joints, bedding planes daylighting into cut face)
morphological: Fluvial or wave erosion undermining the slope toe
Tectonic or steep gravitational escarpment oversteepening
physical_trigger: Prolonged antecedent precipitation and high-intensity storm rainfall
Transient perched groundwater table development and loss of matric suction
human_causes: Anthropogenic excavation / toe undercutting for roadway benching or foundation cuts
Surcharge loading at the slope crest (unengineered spoil disposal or building construction)

usgs_classification.standard_reference: USGS Circular 1325 (Highland & Bobrowsky, 2008) & Cruden & Varnes (1996) TRB Special Report 247

HL-CR-61DC3C62.mitigation_measures:
1. Primary Toe Retention & Structural Retention (IS:14458 Part 2 / MoRTH Section 1500):
   Emergency clearance of 70.7 m³ bulked debris (56.5 m³ in-situ @ 1.25 bulking) followed by construction of a 15m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H_stem = 3.02m, D_f = 1.12m embedment, base width B = 1.44m, concrete volume = 70.40 m³ M15 with 40% plums), backed by 15.85 m³ crushed gravel filter pack wrapped in 64.93 m² non-woven geotextile and 24 Nos. PVC weep holes.
2. Internal Ground Reinforcement & Slope Nailing (MoRTH Section 3100 / CEDD Geoguide 7):
   Installation of 26 Nos. Ø25mm High-Yield Fe500D TMT soil nails (24 working nails + 2 sacrificial test nails) drilled to 9.0m depth (180.0m total drilling), pressure grouted with non-shrink cementitious grout, anchored with RC bearing pads and high-tensile diamond steel wire mesh facing (91.12 m²).
3. Hydrogeological Pore-Pressure Relief & Surface Drainage (MoRTH Section 300, Clause 309 / IRC:SP:48):
   Installation of 5 Nos. × 15m (75.0m total) sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains (Ø75mm, Schedule 80) drilled at 5°–10° upward rake into the hillside, accompanied by crest catch drain, roadside drain, and cascade chute.
4. Soil Bioengineering & Surficial Erosion Control (MoRTH Section 1802 / IS:14458):
   Dressing cut face (91.12 m²), laying 700 GSM coir geotextile netting (110.39 m² with 10% overlap), hydraulic hydroseeding, and planting Vetiver grass contour hedges.
HL-CR-61DC3C62.other_observations: Sub-surface groundwater seepage daylighting along the colluvial mantle and bedrock interface, confirming elevated perched phreatic levels during rainfall. Active extensional tension fissures (apertures 15-40 mm) trace uphill of the detachment crown. Relict discontinuity set J1 (45° dip daylighting adversely into the slope face) exhibits planar persistent slickensides with iron-oxide staining, confirming kinematic daylighting and high susceptibility to progressive retrogressive failure during prolonged monsoon precipitation.

plain_language_explanation.what_happened: A section of the steep hillside has collapsed, depositing soil and rock debris onto the road surface.
plain_language_explanation.why_it_happened: The failure is likely due to the weathering of sandstone and potential saturation of the slope, causing the material to lose stability.
plain_language_explanation.property_and_access_impact: The slide has partially blocked the road, restricting traffic to a single lane and creating a hazard for commuters.
plain_language_explanation.road_and_travel_impact: The slide has partially blocked the road, restricting traffic to a single lane and creating a hazard for commuters.
plain_language_explanation.ongoing_hazards: Risk of secondary rockfall or further sliding remains high until the slope is cleared and stabilized.
plain_language_explanation.what_needs_to_be_done: Clear the debris, perform slope scaling to remove loose rocks, and construct a retaining wall to prevent further encroachment.
plain_language_explanation.citizen_safety_advice: Avoid stopping near the slide area and follow all traffic instructions provided by local authorities.

tier_1_factual_evidence.title: Tier 1: Factual Ground Truth & Telemetry (Objective Past Passive)
tier_1_factual_evidence.description: At Mandi Sector — Hill Road Corridor (Mandi Sector), a detachment scarp of vertical height 7.60 m (upper face 4.90 m inclined at 66°) was surveyed. Saturated shali dolomite & sundernagar quartzite with interbedded phyllitic slate / dharamsala sandstone debris (145.0 m³ in-situ / 181.25 m³ bulked calculated via Simpson's prismoidal rule at 1.25 bulking factor) encroached 2.95 m across the 5.25 m carriageway formation. Roadside drainage was 100% obstructed under active hydrostatic surcharge. Prior to failure, the cut slope was an unprotected excavation. Discontinuities dipping 57° adversely into the slope face were measured with aperture 15–40 mm.

tier_2_analytical_mechanics.title: Tier 2: Analytical Geotechnical Mechanics & FoS (Calibrated Engineering Inferences)
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.description: Under the Cruden & Varnes (1996) and USGS Circular 1325 classification, the failure is designated as a Slide Mass Movement (Cruden & Varnes, 1996) within Shali Dolomite & Sundernagar Quartzite with interbedded phyllitic slate / Dharamsala Sandstone strata. Under dry baseline conditions, limit equilibrium stability analysis (Hoek & Bray planar cleft-water mechanics) yields FoS = 1.01 (marginal). During monsoon steady-seepage saturation with active joint cleft-water hydrostatic pressure (zw = 1.2m), calculated FoS drops to 0.60, confirming active shear mobilization along daylighting joint set J1 (slip plane inclined length L_slip = 6.856 m). Following multi-barrier stabilization, post-remediation FoS is verified at 1.54. The site lies in Seismic Zone V (Z = 0.36, ah = 0.09g).
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.disclaimer: Subsurface geotechnical parameters (effective cohesion c' = 14.0 kPa, effective internal friction angle φ' = 28.0°, intact rock UCS = 35.0 MPa, and structural joint dip = 57.0°) are preliminary model estimates and assumptions based on empirical rock mass classifications and regional lithological analogs. These values are strictly subject to confirmatory site investigation, trial-pit logging, and rotary borehole core extraction with laboratory testing prior to detailed engineering design, statutory tendering, or construction authorization.

tier_3_statutory_directives.title: Tier 3: Statutory Remediation Directives & Civil Schedule (Imperative Standards)
tier_3_statutory_directives.description:
1. Construct a 17m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H_stem=2.70m, D_f=1.00m, Base B=1.35m, Top b=0.60m, volume = 67.70 m³ M15 with 40% plums per IS:14458 Part 2), backed by 16.07 m³ filter pack and 26 Nos. weep holes.
2. Install 20 Nos. Ø25mm High-Yield Fe500D soil nails (18 working in 1.8m H × 2.0m V grid + 2 sacrificial pullout verification test nails) drilled to 9.0m depth (180m drill, 190m bar, 18 pads, 91.12 m² wire mesh) per MoRTH Section 3100.
3. Install 5 Nos. × 15m (75.0m total) sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains (Ø75mm, Schedule 80) at 5°–10° upward rake, paired with 25.0m crest saucer catch drain (0.60m × 0.60m), 17.0m roadside drain (0.60m × 0.60m), and 22.0m stepped cascade chute per MoRTH Section 300.
4. Lay 700 GSM coir geotextile netting (100.23 m² with 10% overlap), hydroseeding, and Vetiver grass contour hedges per MoRTH Section 1802.

usgs_classification.usgs_general_definition: A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement.
usgs_classification.usgs_kinematic_definition: A downslope movement of rock or soil, or both, occurring on the surface of rupture—either curved (rotational slide) or planar (translational slide) rupture—in which much of the material often moves as a coherent or semicoherent mass with little internal deformation.
usgs_classification.material_definition: Soil containing a significant proportion of coarse fragments; 20% to 80% of the particles are greater than 2 mm in size (gravel, cobbles, and boulders).
usgs_classification.movement_definition: A landslide mass that moves out, or down and outward, along a relatively planar surface with little rotational movement or backward tilting; frequently controlled by structural discontinuities (bedding, joints, faults).

velocity_class.consequences: Escape possible; property and structures destroyed; roads severely disrupted.

landslide_anatomy.crown_and_scarp: Undisplaced crown with open extensional crown cracks; distinct steep main scarp exposing rupture surface.
landslide_anatomy.displaced_mass: Depleted mass above planar/rotational surface of rupture, extending downslope into zone of accumulation.
landslide_anatomy.toe_and_foot: Displaced foot advancing beyond toe of rupture surface across roadway/property margin.

geological: Weak, weathered, or fractured rock and soil materials
Adversely oriented structural discontinuities (faults, joints, bedding planes daylighting into cut face)
morphological: Fluvial or wave erosion undermining the slope toe
Tectonic or steep gravitational escarpment oversteepening
physical_trigger: Prolonged antecedent precipitation and high-intensity storm rainfall
Transient perched groundwater table development and loss of matric suction
human_causes: Anthropogenic excavation / toe undercutting for roadway benching or foundation cuts
Surcharge loading at the slope crest (unengineered spoil disposal or building construction)

usgs_classification.standard_reference: USGS Circular 1325 (Highland & Bobrowsky, 2008) & Cruden & Varnes (1996) TRB Special Report 247

usgs_classification.usgs_general_definition: A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement.
usgs_classification.usgs_kinematic_definition: A downslope movement of rock or soil, or both, occurring on the surface of rupture—either curved (rotational slide) or planar (translational slide) rupture—in which much of the material often moves as a coherent or semicoherent mass with little internal deformation.
usgs_classification.material_definition: Soil containing a significant proportion of coarse fragments; 20% to 80% of the particles are greater than 2 mm in size (gravel, cobbles, and boulders).
usgs_classification.movement_definition: A landslide mass that moves out, or down and outward, along a relatively planar surface with little rotational movement or backward tilting; frequently controlled by structural discontinuities (bedding, joints, faults).

velocity_class.consequences: Escape possible; property and structures destroyed; roads severely disrupted.

landslide_anatomy.crown_and_scarp: Undisplaced crown with open extensional crown cracks; distinct steep main scarp exposing rupture surface.
landslide_anatomy.displaced_mass: Depleted mass above planar/rotational surface of rupture, extending downslope into zone of accumulation.
landslide_anatomy.toe_and_foot: Displaced foot advancing beyond toe of rupture surface across roadway/property margin.

geological: Weak, weathered, or fractured rock and soil materials
Adversely oriented structural discontinuities (faults, joints, bedding planes daylighting into cut face)
morphological: Fluvial or wave erosion undermining the slope toe
Tectonic or steep gravitational escarpment oversteepening
physical_trigger: Prolonged antecedent precipitation and high-intensity storm rainfall
Transient perched groundwater table development and loss of matric suction
human_causes: Anthropogenic excavation / toe undercutting for roadway benching or foundation cuts
Surcharge loading at the slope crest (unengineered spoil disposal or building construction)

IITM-STAR-61DC3C62.mitigation_measures:
1. Primary Toe Retention & Structural Retention (IS:14458 Part 2 / MoRTH Section 1500):
   Emergency clearance of 70.7 m³ bulked debris (56.5 m³ in-situ @ 1.25 bulking) followed by construction of a 15m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H_stem = 3.02m, D_f = 1.12m embedment, base width B = 1.44m, concrete volume = 70.40 m³ M15 with 40% plums), backed by 15.85 m³ crushed gravel filter pack wrapped in 64.93 m² non-woven geotextile and 24 Nos. PVC weep holes.
2. Internal Ground Reinforcement & Slope Nailing (MoRTH Section 3100 / CEDD Geoguide 7):
   Installation of 26 Nos. Ø25mm High-Yield Fe500D TMT soil nails (24 working nails + 2 sacrificial test nails) drilled to 9.0m depth (180.0m total drilling), pressure grouted with non-shrink cementitious grout, anchored with RC bearing pads and high-tensile diamond steel wire mesh facing (91.12 m²).
3. Hydrogeological Pore-Pressure Relief & Surface Drainage (MoRTH Section 300, Clause 309 / IRC:SP:48):
   Installation of 5 Nos. × 15m (75.0m total) sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains (Ø75mm, Schedule 80) drilled at 5°–10° upward rake into the hillside, accompanied by crest catch drain, roadside drain, and cascade chute.
4. Soil Bioengineering & Surficial Erosion Control (MoRTH Section 1802 / IS:14458):
   Dressing cut face (91.12 m²), laying 700 GSM coir geotextile netting (110.39 m² with 10% overlap), hydraulic hydroseeding, and planting Vetiver grass contour hedges.
IITM-STAR-61DC3C62.other_observations: Sub-surface groundwater seepage daylighting along the colluvial mantle and bedrock interface, confirming elevated perched phreatic levels during rainfall. Active extensional tension fissures (apertures 15-40 mm) trace uphill of the detachment crown. Relict discontinuity set J1 (45° dip daylighting adversely into the slope face) exhibits planar persistent slickensides with iron-oxide staining, confirming kinematic daylighting and high susceptibility to progressive retrogressive failure during prolonged monsoon precipitation.

tier_1_factual_evidence.title: Tier 1: Factual Ground Truth & Telemetry (Objective Past Passive)
tier_1_factual_evidence.description: At Mandi Sector — Hill Road Corridor (Mandi Sector), a detachment scarp of vertical height 7.60 m (upper face 4.90 m inclined at 66°) was surveyed. Saturated shali dolomite & sundernagar quartzite with interbedded phyllitic slate / dharamsala sandstone debris (145.0 m³ in-situ / 181.25 m³ bulked calculated via Simpson's prismoidal rule at 1.25 bulking factor) encroached 2.95 m across the 5.25 m carriageway formation. Roadside drainage was 100% obstructed under active hydrostatic surcharge. Prior to failure, the cut slope was an unprotected excavation. Discontinuities dipping 57° adversely into the slope face were measured with aperture 15–40 mm.

tier_2_analytical_mechanics.title: Tier 2: Analytical Geotechnical Mechanics & FoS (Calibrated Engineering Inferences)
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.description: Under the Cruden & Varnes (1996) and USGS Circular 1325 classification, the failure is designated as a Slide Mass Movement (Cruden & Varnes, 1996) within Shali Dolomite & Sundernagar Quartzite with interbedded phyllitic slate / Dharamsala Sandstone strata. Under dry baseline conditions, limit equilibrium stability analysis (Hoek & Bray planar cleft-water mechanics) yields FoS = 1.01 (marginal). During monsoon steady-seepage saturation with active joint cleft-water hydrostatic pressure (zw = 1.2m), calculated FoS drops to 0.60, confirming active shear mobilization along daylighting joint set J1 (slip plane inclined length L_slip = 6.856 m). Following multi-barrier stabilization, post-remediation FoS is verified at 1.54. The site lies in Seismic Zone V (Z = 0.36, ah = 0.09g).
tier_2_analytical_mechanics.disclaimer: Subsurface geotechnical parameters (effective cohesion c' = 14.0 kPa, effective internal friction angle φ' = 28.0°, intact rock UCS = 35.0 MPa, and structural joint dip = 57.0°) are preliminary model estimates and assumptions based on empirical rock mass classifications and regional lithological analogs. These values are strictly subject to confirmatory site investigation, trial-pit logging, and rotary borehole core extraction with laboratory testing prior to detailed engineering design, statutory tendering, or construction authorization.

tier_3_statutory_directives.title: Tier 3: Statutory Remediation Directives & Civil Schedule (Imperative Standards)
tier_3_statutory_directives.description:
1. Construct a 17m long Plum Concrete Breast Wall (H_stem=2.70m, D_f=1.00m, Base B=1.35m, Top b=0.60m, volume = 67.70 m³ M15 with 40% plums per IS:14458 Part 2), backed by 16.07 m³ filter pack and 26 Nos. weep holes.
2. Install 20 Nos. Ø25mm High-Yield Fe500D soil nails (18 working in 1.8m H × 2.0m V grid + 2 sacrificial pullout verification test nails) drilled to 9.0m depth (180m drill, 190m bar, 18 pads, 91.12 m² wire mesh) per MoRTH Section 3100.
3. Install 5 Nos. × 15m (75.0m total) sub-horizontal slotted PVC relief drains (Ø75mm, Schedule 80) at 5°–10° upward rake, paired with 25.0m crest saucer catch drain (0.60m × 0.60m), 17.0m roadside drain (0.60m × 0.60m), and 22.0m stepped cascade chute per MoRTH Section 300.
4. Lay 700 GSM coir geotextile netting (100.23 m² with 10% overlap), hydroseeding, and Vetiver grass contour hedges per MoRTH Section 1802.

usgs_classification.usgs_general_definition: A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement.
usgs_classification.usgs_kinematic_definition: A downslope movement of rock or soil, or both, occurring on the surface of rupture—either curved (rotational slide) or planar (translational slide) rupture—in which much of the material often moves as a coherent or semicoherent mass with little internal deformation.
usgs_classification.material_definition: Soil containing a significant proportion of coarse fragments; 20% to 80% of the particles are greater than 2 mm in size (gravel, cobbles, and boulders).
usgs_classification.movement_definition: A landslide mass that moves out, or down and outward, along a relatively planar surface with little rotational movement or backward tilting; frequently controlled by structural discontinuities (bedding, joints, faults).

landslide_anatomy.crown_and_scarp: Undisplaced crown with open extensional crown cracks; distinct steep main scarp exposing rupture surface.
landslide_anatomy.displaced_mass: Depleted mass above planar/rotational surface of rupture, extending downslope into zone of accumulation.
landslide_anatomy.toe_and_foot: Displaced foot advancing beyond toe of rupture surface across roadway/property margin.

geological: Weak, weathered, or fractured rock and soil materials
Adversely oriented structural discontinuities (faults, joints, bedding planes daylighting into cut face)
morphological: Fluvial or wave erosion undermining the slope toe
Tectonic or steep gravitational escarpment oversteepening
physical_trigger: Prolonged antecedent precipitation and high-intensity storm rainfall
Transient perched groundwater table development and loss of matric suction
human_causes: Anthropogenic excavation / toe undercutting for roadway benching or foundation cuts
Surcharge loading at the slope crest (unengineered spoil disposal or building construction)

usgs_classification.standard_reference: USGS Circular 1325 (Highland & Bobrowsky, 2008) & Cruden & Varnes (1996) TRB Special Report 247

nature_based_solution.description: Hollow box-like interlocking timber or precast concrete beam framework backfilled with soil/rock and planted with live root cuttings.

usgs_classification.usgs_general_definition: A landslide is a general term used to describe the downslope movement of soil, rock, and organic materials under the effects of gravity and also the landform that results from such movement.
usgs_classification.usgs_kinematic_definition: A downslope movement of rock or soil, or both, occurring on the surface of rupture—either curved (rotational slide) or planar (translational slide) rupture—in which much of the material often moves as a coherent or semicoherent mass with little internal deformation.
usgs_classification.material_definition: Soil containing a significant proportion of coarse fragments; 20% to 80% of the particles are greater than 2 mm in size (gravel, cobbles, and boulders).
usgs_classification.movement_definition: A landslide mass that moves out, or down and outward, along a relatively planar surface with little rotational movement or backward tilting; frequently controlled by structural discontinuities (bedding, joints, faults).

velocity_class.consequences: Escape possible; property and structures destroyed; roads severely disrupted.
